bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑第068卷

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 68
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 68

sentences.zh: 【漢紀六十】起強圍作噩，盡屠維大淵獻，凡三年。

translations.literal: [Han Records 60] Beginning with Qiangwei Zuoe, ending with Tuwei Dayuanxian, three years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Han Records 60] Spanning from the year Qiangwei Zuoe through Tuwei Dayuanxian—a period of three years.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，魏王操軍居巢，孫權保濡須，二月，操進攻之。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, King Cao of Wei's army was at Juchao; Sun Quan held Ruxu. Second month, Cao advanced to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, during the first month, King Cao Cao of Wei encamped at Juchao while Sun Quan defended Ruxu. In the second month, Cao advanced to attack him.

sentences.zh: 初，右護軍蔣欽屯宣城，蕪湖令徐盛收欽屯吏，表斬之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jiang Qin of the Right Guards Army was garrisoned at Xuancheng. Xu Sheng, magistrate of Wuhu, arrested an officer from Qin's camp and memorialized that he be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Jiang Qin of the Right Guards Army had been stationed at Xuancheng. Xu Sheng, the magistrate of Wuhu, arrested one of Qin's garrison officers and submitted a memorial requesting his execution.

sentences.zh: 及權在濡須，欽與呂蒙持諸軍節度，欽每稱徐盛之善。

translations.literal: When Quan was at Ruxu, Qin and Lü Meng held command over the various armies' discipline. Qin often praised Xu Sheng's merits.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan was at Ruxu, Jiang Qin and Lü Meng oversaw military discipline among the armies, and Qin repeatedly spoke of Xu Sheng's excellence.

sentences.zh: 權問之，欽曰：「盛忠而勤強，有膽略器用，好萬人督也。

translations.literal: Quan asked him about it. Qin said: "Sheng is loyal and diligent and strong, possessed of courage, strategy, and ability—well suited to command ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan asked him about this. Qin replied, "Sheng is loyal, diligent, and formidable, with courage, strategy, and real ability—he is well suited to command ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 今大事未定，臣當助國求才，豈敢挾私恨以蔽賢乎！

translations.literal: Now the great enterprise is not yet settled; your servant ought to help the state seek talent—how would I dare harbor private resentment to conceal the worthy!
translations.idiomatic: The great enterprise is not yet settled; I ought to help the state find talent. How could I let private resentment hide a worthy man from you!

sentences.zh: 」權善之。

translations.literal: " Quan approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: " Sun Quan commended him for it.

sentences.zh: 三月，操引軍還，留伏波將軍夏侯惇都督曹仁、張遼等二十六軍屯居巢。

translations.literal: Third month, Cao led his army back, leaving General Who Calms the Waves Xiahou Dun to supervise Cao Ren, Zhang Liao, and twenty-six other armies garrisoned at Juchao.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Cao withdrew his army, leaving General Who Calms the Waves Xiahou Dun to command Cao Ren, Zhang Liao, and twenty-six other armies encamped at Juchao.

sentences.zh: 權令都尉徐詳詣操請降，操報使修好，誓重結婚。

translations.literal: Quan ordered Commandant Xu Xiang to go to Cao to request submission. Cao replied that they should restore friendly relations and swear anew to ally by marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan sent Commandant Xu Xiang to Cao to offer submission. Cao responded that they should restore friendly relations and renew their oath of alliance by marriage.

sentences.zh: 權留平虜將軍周泰督濡須；

translations.literal: Quan left General Who Pacifies the Barbarians Zhou Tai to supervise Ruxu;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan left General Who Pacifies the Barbarians Zhou Tai in command at Ruxu;

sentences.zh: 朱然、徐盛等皆在所部，以泰寒門，不服。

translations.literal: Zhu Ran, Xu Sheng, and others were all under his command, but because Tai came from a humble family, they would not submit to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ran, Xu Sheng, and others all served under him, yet because Zhou Tai came from a humble background, they refused to accept his authority.

sentences.zh: 權會諸將，大為酣樂，命泰解衣，權手自指其創痕，問以所起，泰輒記昔戰鬥處以對。

translations.literal: Quan gathered the generals for great revelry and merriment, ordered Tai to remove his clothes, and with his own hand pointed to each scar, asking where each came from; Tai would recall the place of each past battle to answer.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan summoned the generals for a great feast and ordered Zhou Tai to bare his torso. Sun Quan himself pointed to each scar and asked how it had been received; Tai named the battle in which he had received each wound.

sentences.zh: 畢，使復服；

translations.literal: When finished, he had him dress again;
translations.idiomatic: When this was finished, he had Tai dress again;

sentences.zh: 權把其臂流涕曰：「幼平，卿為孤兄弟，戰如熊虎，不惜軀命，被創數十，膚如刻畫，孤亦何心不待卿以骨肉之恩，委卿以兵馬之重乎？

translations.literal: Quan grasped his arm and wept, saying: "Youping, you have been a brother to me in battle, fighting like bear and tiger, sparing not your life—you have received wounds by the dozens, your skin like carved lines. How could I lack the heart to treat you with the kindness due kin and entrust you with the weight of arms and horses?
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan seized his arm with tears and said, "Youping, you have fought for me as a brother, battling like bear and tiger without sparing your life. You have taken dozens of wounds until your skin looks carved in lines. With what heart could I fail to treat you with the kindness owed to kin, or entrust you with command of troops and horses?

sentences.zh: 」坐罷，住駕，使泰以兵馬道從，鳴鼓角作鼓吹而出。

translations.literal: " When the gathering ended, he halted his carriage and had Tai follow with troops and horses, sounding drums, horns, and martial music as they went out.
translations.idiomatic: " When the feast ended, he halted his carriage and had Zhou Tai follow with troops and horses, drums and horns sounding and martial music playing as they departed.

sentences.zh: 於是盛等乃服。

translations.literal: Thereupon Sheng and the others submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Xu Sheng and the others submit to Zhou Tai's authority.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，語魏王操設天子旌旗，出入稱警蹕。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, an edict ordered King Cao to set up the imperial banners and flags; on going out and coming in he was to be announced with the imperial guard cry.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, during the fourth month, an edict authorized King Cao to display the imperial banners and flags and to be announced with the imperial guard cry whenever he went abroad.

sentences.zh: 六月，魏以軍師華歆為御史大夫。

translations.literal: Sixth month, Wei appointed Military Adviser Hua Xin as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Wei appointed Military Adviser Hua Xin Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，命魏王操冕十有二旒，乘金根車，駕六馬，設五時副車。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, King Cao was ordered a crown with twelve tassels, to ride the golden-root carriage, drive six horses, and have five seasonal secondary carriages.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, during the tenth month, King Cao was granted a twelve-tassel crown, the golden-root carriage drawn by six horses, and five seasonal secondary carriages.

sentences.zh: 魏以五官中郎將丕為太子。

translations.literal: Wei made Palace Attendant of the Five Offices Pi crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Wei named Palace Attendant of the Five Offices Cao Pi crown prince.

sentences.zh: 初，魏王操娶丁夫人，無子；

translations.literal: Initially, King Cao took Lady Ding as wife; she had no sons;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, King Cao had married Lady Ding, who bore him no sons;

sentences.zh: 妾劉氏，生子昂；

translations.literal: a concubine, Lady Liu, bore Ang;
translations.idiomatic: his concubine Lady Liu bore Cao Ang;

sentences.zh: 卞氏生四子：丕、彰、植、熊。

translations.literal: Lady Bian bore four sons: Pi, Zhang, Zhi, and Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Bian bore four sons: Pi, Zhang, Zhi, and Xiong.

sentences.zh: 王使丁夫人母養昂。

translations.literal: The king had Lady Ding raise Ang as her own.
translations.idiomatic: The king had Lady Ding raise Ang as her own son.

sentences.zh: 昂死於穰，丁夫人哭泣無節，操怒而出之，以卞氏為繼室。

translations.literal: Ang died at Rang; Lady Ding wept without restraint. Cao in anger sent her away and made Lady Bian his successor wife.
translations.idiomatic: When Ang died at Rang, Lady Ding mourned without restraint. Cao in anger dismissed her and made Lady Bian his principal consort.

sentences.zh: 植性機警，多藝能，才藻敏贍，操愛之。

translations.literal: Zhi by nature was quick-witted, possessed of many arts and skills, his literary talent keen and ample; Cao loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was quick-witted and multitalented, with keen and abundant literary gifts, and Cao favored him greatly.

sentences.zh: 操欲以女妻丁儀，丕以儀目眇，諫止之。

translations.literal: Cao wished to give his daughter in marriage to Ding Yi; Pi, because Yi was blind in one eye, remonstrated and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: Cao wished to marry his daughter to Ding Yi, but Pi objected on the grounds that Yi was blind in one eye and persuaded his father to abandon the match.

sentences.zh: 儀由是怨丕，與弟黃門侍郎廙及丞相主簿楊修，數稱臨菑侯植之才，勸操立以為嗣。

translations.literal: Yi thereby resented Pi. Together with his younger brother Yellow Gate Attendant Yi and the Chancellor's Registrar Yang Xiu, he repeatedly praised the talent of Marquis of Linzi Zhi and urged Cao to establish him as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Yi therefore bore a grudge against Pi. Together with his younger brother Yellow Gate Attendant Ding Yi and the Chancellor's Registrar Yang Xiu, he repeatedly praised the Marquis of Linzi's talents and urged Cao to name Zhi his heir.

sentences.zh: 修，彪之子也。

translations.literal: Xiu was the son of Biao.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiu was the son of Yang Biao.

sentences.zh: 操以函密訪於外，尚書崔琰露板答曰：「《春秋》之義，立子以長。

translations.literal: Cao made secret inquiries abroad in sealed letters. Minister of the Masters of Writing Cui Yan posted an open reply: "The meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals is to establish the son who is eldest.
translations.idiomatic: Cao made secret inquiries in sealed letters to officials outside. Minister of the Masters of Writing Cui Yan posted a public reply: "The Spring and Autumn Annals teach that the eldest son should be established.

sentences.zh: 加五官將仁孝聰明，宜承正統，琰以死守之。

translations.literal: Moreover the Palace Attendant of the Five Offices is benevolent, filial, and intelligent—fit to inherit the legitimate succession; Yan will defend this to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Palace Attendant of the Five Offices is benevolent, filial, and intelligent—fit to inherit the legitimate succession. I will defend this position to the death.

sentences.zh: 」植，琰之兄女婿也。

translations.literal: " Zhi was the son-in-law of Yan's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhi was married to the daughter of Yan's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 尚書僕射毛玠曰：「近者袁紹以嫡庶不分，覆宗滅國。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Mao Jie said: "Recently Yuan Shao, because legitimate and secondary sons were not distinguished, overturned his clan and destroyed his state.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Mao Jie said, "Not long ago Yuan Shao failed to distinguish legitimate from secondary heirs, and his clan was overturned and his state destroyed.

sentences.zh: 廢立大事，非所宜聞。

translations.literal: The great matter of deposing and establishing is not what one should hear discussed.
translations.idiomatic: The great matter of deposing and establishing an heir is not something that should even be discussed.

sentences.zh: 」東曹掾邢顒曰：「以庶代宗，先世之戒也，願殿下深察之。

translations.literal: " Eastern Bureau Aide Xing Yong said: "To replace the legitimate heir with a secondary son is a warning from former ages; I hope Your Highness will examine this deeply.
translations.idiomatic: " Eastern Bureau Aide Xing Yong said, "Replacing the legitimate heir with a secondary son is a warning drawn from former ages. I hope Your Highness will consider this carefully.

sentences.zh: 」丕使人問太中大夫賈詡以自固之術。

translations.literal: " Pi sent someone to ask Grand Master of the Palace Jia Xu for a method to secure his own position.
translations.idiomatic: " Cao Pi sent someone to ask Grand Master of the Palace Jia Xu how he might secure his own position.

sentences.zh: 詡曰：「願將軍恢崇德度，躬素士之業，朝夕孜孜，不違子道，如此而已。

translations.literal: Xu said: "I hope the General will expand and honor virtue and magnanimity, personally undertake the duties of a plain scholar, morning and evening diligent and untiring, not departing from the way of a son—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Xu replied, "I hope the General will broaden his virtue and magnanimity, personally devote himself to the duties of a plain scholar, and work diligently morning and evening without departing from the way of a son. That is all there is to it.

sentences.zh: 」丕從之，深自砥礪。

translations.literal: " Pi followed this and deeply disciplined himself.
translations.idiomatic: " Cao Pi took this advice and redoubled his self-discipline.

sentences.zh: 它日，操屏人問詡，詡嘿然不對。

translations.literal: Another day, Cao dismissed attendants and questioned Xu; Xu was silent and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion, Cao dismissed his attendants and questioned Jia Xu, but Xu remained silent and would not reply.

sentences.zh: 操曰：「與卿言，而不答，何也？

translations.literal: Cao said: "I speak with you, yet you do not answer—why?
translations.idiomatic: Cao said, "I am speaking with you, yet you will not answer. Why?

sentences.zh: 」詡曰：「屬有所思，故不即對耳。

translations.literal: " Xu said: "I was just then thinking of something, and so did not reply at once.
translations.idiomatic: " Jia Xu said, "I was thinking of something just then and so did not reply at once.

sentences.zh: 」操曰：「何思？

translations.literal: " Cao said: "What were you thinking of?
translations.idiomatic: " Cao asked, "What were you thinking of?

sentences.zh: 」詡曰：「思袁本初、劉景升父子也。

translations.literal: " Xu said: "I was thinking of Yuan Benchu and Liu Jingsheng, father and sons.
translations.idiomatic: " Jia Xu replied, "I was thinking of Yuan Shao and Liu Biao, and what became of their sons.

sentences.zh: 」操大笑。

translations.literal: " Cao laughed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: " Cao burst out laughing.

sentences.zh: 操嘗出征，丕、植並送路側，植稱述功德，發言有章，左右屬目，操亦悅焉。

translations.literal: Cao once went on campaign; Pi and Zhi both saw him off by the roadside. Zhi recounted his achievements and merits; his speech was well ordered, and those left and right fixed their eyes on him; Cao too was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Once when Cao set out on campaign, Pi and Zhi both saw him off along the road. Zhi recounted his father's achievements in polished, well-ordered speech that drew every eye, and Cao was pleased.

sentences.zh: 丕悵然自失，濟陰吳質耳語曰：「王當行，流涕可也。

translations.literal: Pi was despondent and felt himself at a loss. Wu Zhi of Jiyin whispered in his ear: "When the king is about to depart, shedding tears will do.
translations.idiomatic: Pi was despondent and felt himself losing ground. Wu Zhi of Jiyin whispered in his ear, "When the king is about to depart, tears would serve you well.

sentences.zh: 」及辭，丕涕泣而拜，操及左右鹹歔欷，於是皆以植多華辭而誠心不及也。

translations.literal: " When taking leave, Pi wept and bowed; Cao and those left and right all sighed and sobbed. Thereupon all judged that Zhi had too much flowery speech while his sincere heart did not measure up.
translations.idiomatic: " When the time came to take leave, Pi wept as he bowed farewell, and Cao and everyone around him sighed and sobbed. From that point on, all concluded that Zhi's words were too ornate while his sincerity did not measure up.

sentences.zh: 植既任性而行，不自雕飾，五官將御之以術，矯情自飾，宮人左右並為之稱說，故遂定為太子。

translations.literal: Zhi, being willful in conduct, did not adorn himself; the Palace Attendant of the Five Offices countered him with stratagems, feigning emotion to adorn himself, and the palace attendants left and right all praised him on his behalf—thus the heir was finally settled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi acted willfully and made no effort to polish his conduct, while the Palace Attendant of the Five Offices countered with stratagems, feigning emotion to adorn himself, and the palace attendants on every side praised him—thus the heir was finally settled on Pi.

sentences.zh: 左右長御賀卞夫人曰：「將軍拜太子，天下莫不喜，夫人當傾府藏以賞賜。

translations.literal: The attendants and chief stewards congratulated Lady Bian, saying: "The General has been made crown prince—all under Heaven rejoice; the Lady ought to empty the treasury stores for rewards.
translations.idiomatic: The attendants and chief stewards congratulated Lady Bian, saying, "The General has been named crown prince, and all under Heaven rejoices. You ought to empty the treasury stores for rewards.

sentences.zh: 」夫人曰：「王自以丕年大，故用為嗣。

translations.literal: " The Lady said: "The King himself, because Pi is the elder, therefore used him as heir.
translations.idiomatic: " Lady Bian replied, "The King himself chose Pi as heir because he is the elder.

sentences.zh: 我但當以免無教導之過為幸耳，亦何為當重賜遺乎？

translations.literal: I should only count it fortunate to escape the fault of having failed to instruct him—why should I make heavy gifts and rewards?
translations.idiomatic: I should count myself fortunate merely to escape blame for having failed to instruct him properly. Why should I make lavish gifts and rewards?

sentences.zh: 」長御還，具以語操，操悅，曰：「怒不變容，喜不失節，故最為難。

translations.literal: " The chief steward returned and reported all this to Cao in detail. Cao was pleased and said: "Not changing countenance in anger, not losing propriety in joy—that is what is most difficult.
translations.idiomatic: " The chief steward returned and reported her words in full to Cao. Cao was pleased and said, "Not changing countenance in anger and not losing propriety in joy—that is what is most difficult.

sentences.zh: 」太子抱議郎辛毘頸而言曰：「辛君知我喜不？

translations.literal: " The crown prince embraced Registrar Xin Pi by the neck and said: "Master Xin, do you know whether I am pleased?
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince threw his arms around Registrar Xin Pi's neck and said, "Master Xin, can you tell whether I am pleased?

sentences.zh: 」毘以告其女憲英，憲英歎曰：「太子，代君主宗廟、社稷者也。

translations.literal: " Pi told his daughter Xianying. Xianying sighed and said: "The crown prince is one who stands in for the ruler to tend the ancestral temples and altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: " Xin Pi told his daughter Xianying. Xianying sighed and said, "The crown prince stands in for the ruler to tend the ancestral temples and the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 代君，不可以不戚；

translations.literal: Standing in for the ruler, one cannot but be sorrowful;
translations.idiomatic: Standing in for the ruler, one ought to feel sorrow;

sentences.zh: 主國，不可以不懼。

translations.literal: holding the state, one cannot but be fearful.
translations.idiomatic: and holding charge of the state, one ought to feel fear.

sentences.zh: 宜戚宜懼，而反以為喜，何以能久！

translations.literal: One ought to be sorrowful and fearful, yet instead takes it as joy—how can this last long!
translations.idiomatic: He ought to feel sorrow and fear, yet instead he treats it as joy. How can such a state endure for long!

sentences.zh: 魏其不昌乎！

translations.literal: Will not Wei fail to flourish!
translations.idiomatic: Surely Wei will not long prosper!

sentences.zh: 」久之，臨菑侯植乘車行馳道中，開司馬門出。

translations.literal: " After some time, the Marquis of Linzi Zhi drove his carriage along the imperial thoroughfare and opened the Major's Gate to go out.
translations.idiomatic: " Some time later, the Marquis of Linzi drove his carriage along the imperial thoroughfare and opened the Major's Gate to pass through.

sentences.zh: 操大怒，公車令坐死。

translations.literal: Cao was greatly angered; the Director of the Imperial Carriages was sentenced to death for the offense.
translations.idiomatic: Cao was furious and had the Director of the Imperial Carriages executed for the offense.

sentences.zh: 由是重諸侯科禁，而植寵日衰。

translations.literal: From this he redoubled the regulations and prohibitions on feudal lords, while Zhi's favor daily declined.
translations.idiomatic: From this he tightened the regulations governing feudal lords, while Zhi's favor declined day by day.

sentences.zh: 植妻衣繡，操登台見之，以違制命，還家賜死。

translations.literal: Zhi's wife wore embroidered clothing. Cao ascended a tower and saw her; because this violated regulations, he sent her home and granted her death.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's wife wore embroidered robes. Cao saw her from a tower, judged the dress a violation of regulations, and ordered her sent home and put to death.

sentences.zh: 法正說劉備曰：「曹操一舉而降張魯，定漢中，不因此勢以圖巴、蜀，而留夏侯淵、張郃屯守，身遽北還，此非其智不逮而力不足也，必將內有憂逼故耳。

translations.literal: Fa Zheng urged Liu Bei, saying: "Cao Cao in one move subdued Zhang Lu and settled Hanzhong. He did not use this momentum to take Ba and Shu, but left Xiahou Yuan and Zhang He to garrison and defend while he himself hurried north—this is not because his wisdom fell short or his strength was insufficient; he must have had pressing troubles within.
translations.idiomatic: Fa Zheng urged Liu Bei, saying, "Cao Cao subdued Zhang Lu and secured Hanzhong in a single campaign. He did not use that momentum to seize Ba and Shu, but left Xiahou Yuan and Zhang He to garrison the region while he himself hurried north. This is not because his wisdom or strength fell short—he must have been pressed by troubles at home.

sentences.zh: 今策淵、郃才略，不勝國之將帥，舉眾往討，必可克之。

translations.literal: Now if we gauge Yuan and He's talent and strategy, they do not match a state's generals and commanders. If we raise the host to attack, we can surely overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Judging Yuan and He by their talent and strategy, they cannot match the foremost generals of a great state. If we march against them in force, we are sure to prevail.

sentences.zh: 克之之日，廣農積穀，觀釁伺隙，上可以傾覆寇敵，尊獎王室；

translations.literal: On the day of victory, expand agriculture and store grain, watch for openings and await gaps—in the upper reach, overturn the enemy invaders and honor and aid the royal house;
translations.idiomatic: Once we prevail, we should expand agriculture and store grain, watch for openings and await our chance. At the highest level, we could overturn the enemy and restore honor to the royal house;

sentences.zh: 中可以蠶食雍、涼，廣拓境土；

translations.literal: in the middle, nibble away Yong and Liang and broadly extend territory;
translations.idiomatic: at the middle level, nibble away at Yong and Liang and greatly extend our territory;

sentences.zh: 下可以固守要害，為持久之計。

translations.literal: in the lower, firmly hold key points and make a plan for endurance.
translations.idiomatic: and at the lowest level, hold the strategic passes and make plans for a long war.

sentences.zh: 此蓋天以與我，時不可失也。

translations.literal: This is surely Heaven giving it to us—the time cannot be lost.
translations.idiomatic: Surely Heaven has given us this opportunity, and the moment must not be lost.

sentences.zh: 」備善其策，乃率諸將進兵漢中，遣張飛、馬超、吳蘭等屯下辨。

translations.literal: " Bei approved of this plan and thereupon led the generals to advance on Hanzhong, sending Zhang Fei, Ma Chao, Wu Lan, and others to garrison Xiabian.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Bei approved the plan and led his generals into Hanzhong, sending Zhang Fei, Ma Chao, Wu Lan, and others to garrison Xiabian.

sentences.zh: 魏王操遣都護將軍曹洪拒之。

translations.literal: King Cao of Wei sent Chief Commandant General Cao Hong to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: King Cao sent Chief Commandant General Cao Hong to resist him.

sentences.zh: 魯肅卒，孫權以從事中郎彭城嚴畯代肅，督兵萬人鎮陸口。

translations.literal: Lu Su died. Sun Quan made Attendant of Affairs Pengcheng Yan Jun replace Su, supervising ten thousand troops to garrison Lukou.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Su died, Sun Quan appointed Attendant of Affairs Yan Jun of Pengcheng to replace him, placing ten thousand troops under his command to garrison Lukou.

sentences.zh: 眾人皆為畯喜，畯固辭以「樸素書生，不閒軍事」，發言懇惻，至於流涕。

translations.literal: Everyone rejoiced for Jun, but Jun firmly declined on the grounds that he was "a plain and simple scholar, unskilled in military affairs," his words earnest and sincere, even to the point of shedding tears.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone congratulated Yan Jun, but he firmly declined on the grounds that he was "a plain scholar unversed in military affairs," speaking with such earnest sincerity that he wept.

sentences.zh: 權乃以左護軍虎威將軍呂蒙兼漢昌太守以代之。

translations.literal: Quan thereupon made Left Guards Army Tiger Might General Lü Meng also Administrator of Hanchang to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan then appointed Left Guards Army Tiger Might General Lü Meng, who also served as Administrator of Hanchang, to replace him.

sentences.zh: 眾嘉嚴畯能以實讓。

translations.literal: The multitude praised Yan Jun for being able to yield in truth.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone praised Yan Jun for yielding the post when he knew himself unfit for it.

sentences.zh: 定威校尉吳郡陸遜言於孫權曰：「方今克敵寧亂，非眾不濟；

translations.literal: Establishing Might Commandant Lu Xun of Wu Commandery said to Sun Quan: "At present to overcome enemies and pacify disorder, without the multitude it cannot succeed;
translations.idiomatic: Establishing Might Commandant Lu Xun of Wu Commandery said to Sun Quan, "To overcome enemies and pacify disorder today, we cannot succeed without numbers;

sentences.zh: 而山寇舊惡，依阻深地。

translations.literal: yet the mountain bandits are an old evil, relying on barriers in deep country.
translations.idiomatic: yet the mountain bandits remain an old scourge, entrenched in rugged, remote terrain.

sentences.zh: 夫腹心未平，難以圖遠，可大部伍，取其精銳。

translations.literal: When the heart and belly are not yet pacified, it is hard to plan for distant goals. We may greatly organize troops and take their elite and sharp.
translations.idiomatic: While our own heartland is not yet secure, it is hard to plan distant campaigns. We should organize large forces and take their best fighters.

sentences.zh: 」權從之，以為帳下右都督。

translations.literal: " Quan followed this and made him Right Commander-in-Chief under his tent.
translations.idiomatic: " Sun Quan followed his advice and appointed him Right Commander-in-Chief on his staff.

sentences.zh: 會丹楊賊帥費棧作亂，扇動山越。

translations.literal: It happened that Danyang bandit chief Fei Zhan rebelled, stirring up the Shanyue.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Danyang bandit chief Fei Zhan rebelled and stirred up the Shanyue.

sentences.zh: 權命遜討棧，破之。

translations.literal: Quan ordered Xun to attack Zhan and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan ordered Lu Xun to attack Zhan and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 遂部伍東三郡，強者為兵，羸者補戶，得精卒數萬人。

translations.literal: He then organized the three eastern commanderies into ranks: the strong became soldiers, the weak supplemented households, and obtained elite troops numbering in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He then organized the three eastern commanderies: the able-bodied were enrolled as soldiers, the weak were assigned to households, and he obtained several tens of thousands of elite troops.

sentences.zh: 宿惡蕩除，所過肅清，還屯蕪湖。

translations.literal: Long-standing evils were swept away; wherever he passed was cleared and made orderly; he returned to garrison at Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: Long-standing evils were swept away, every district he passed was pacified, and he returned to garrison at Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 會稽太守淳-{于}-式表「遜枉取民人，愁擾所在。

translations.literal: Kuaiji Administrator Chunyu Shi memorialized: "Xun wrongly took the people, causing grief and disturbance wherever he went.
translations.idiomatic: Kuaiji Administrator Chunyu Shi submitted a memorial stating that "Lu Xun had wrongly seized the people, causing grief and disturbance wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 」遜後詣都，言次，稱式佳吏。

translations.literal: " Later Xun came to the capital; in the course of conversation he praised Shi as an excellent official.
translations.idiomatic: " Later, when Lu Xun came to the capital, he praised Chunyu Shi in conversation as an excellent official.

sentences.zh: 權曰：「式白君，而君薦之，何也？

translations.literal: Quan said: "Shi reported against you, yet you recommend him—why?
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan asked, "Shi reported against you, yet you recommend him. Why?

sentences.zh: 」遜對曰：「式意欲養民，是以白遜。

translations.literal: " Xun replied: "Shi's intent was to nurture the people; that is why he reported against Xun.
translations.idiomatic: " Lu Xun replied, "His intent was to protect the people, and that is why he reported against me.

sentences.zh: 若遜復毀式以亂聖聽，不可長也。

translations.literal: If Xun were again to slander Shi and confuse the sage hearing, that cannot be long endured.
translations.idiomatic: If I were now to slander him in turn and confuse Your Majesty's judgment, such conduct cannot be tolerated for long.

sentences.zh: 」權曰：「此誠長者之事，顧人不能為耳。

translations.literal: " Quan said: "This is truly the conduct of a man of mature virtue—only ordinary people cannot do it.
translations.idiomatic: " Sun Quan said, "That is truly the conduct of a man of mature virtue—ordinary men simply cannot do such a thing.

sentences.zh: 魏王操使丞相長史王必典兵督許中事。

translations.literal: King Cao of Wei sent the Chancellor's Chief Clerk Wang Bi to command troops and supervise affairs in Xu.
translations.idiomatic: King Cao sent the Chancellor's Chief Clerk Wang Bi to command troops and supervise affairs at Xu.

sentences.zh: 時關羽強盛，京兆金禕睹漢祚將移，乃與少府耿紀、司直韋晃、太醫令吉本、本子邈、邈弟穆等謀殺必，挾天子以攻魏，南引關羽為援。

translations.literal: At this time Guan Yu was powerful. Jin Yi of Jingzhao, seeing that the Han mandate was about to shift, thereupon with Palace Treasurer Geng Ji, Director of Standards Wei Huang, Grand Physician Ji Ben, the heir's son Miao, and Miao's younger brother Mu and others plotted to kill Bi, seize the Son of Heaven to attack Wei, and draw Guan Yu from the south as support.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Guan Yu was at the height of his power. Jin Yi of Jingzhao, seeing that the Han mandate was slipping away, joined Palace Treasurer Geng Ji, Director of Standards Wei Huang, Grand Physician Ji Ben, the heir's son Ji Miao, Miao's younger brother Ji Mu, and others in a plot to kill Wang Bi, seize the emperor to attack Wei, and draw Guan Yu from the south as their ally.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，吉邈等率其黨千餘人，夜攻王必，燒其門，射必中肩，帳下督扶必奔南城。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, Ji Miao and the others led their faction of more than a thousand men to attack Wang Bi by night, burned his gate, and shot Bi in the shoulder. The tent supervisor supported Bi and fled to the southern city.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, during the first month, Ji Miao and his followers, more than a thousand strong, attacked Wang Bi by night, burned his gate, and shot him in the shoulder. Bi's tent supervisor helped him flee to the southern city.

sentences.zh: 會天明，邈等眾潰，必與穎川典農中郎將嚴匡共討斬之。

translations.literal: When dawn came, Miao and the others' host scattered. Bi together with Yingchuan Director of Agriculture Zhonglang General Yan Kuang jointly pursued and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak their forces scattered. Wang Bi joined Yingchuan Director of Agriculture Zhonglang General Yan Kuang in pursuing them and had them executed.

sentences.zh: 三月，有星孛於東方。

translations.literal: Third month, a broom star appeared in the east.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, a comet appeared in the eastern sky.

sentences.zh: 曹洪將擊吳蘭，張飛屯固山，聲言欲斷軍後，眾議狐疑。

translations.literal: Cao Hong was about to attack Wu Lan. Zhang Fei was garrisoned at Gushan, proclaiming that he intended to cut off the army's rear; the assembly's counsel was doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Hong was preparing to attack Wu Lan when Zhang Fei encamped at Gushan and proclaimed that he intended to cut off the army's rear, leaving the command uncertain what to do.

sentences.zh: 騎都尉曹休曰：「賊實斷道者，當伏兵潛行；

translations.literal: Cavalry Commandant Cao Xiu said: "If bandits truly meant to cut the road, they should deploy hidden troops and move in secret;
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry Commandant Cao Xiu said, "If the enemy truly meant to cut our supply line, they would move hidden troops in secret;

sentences.zh: 今乃先張聲勢，此其不能，明矣。

translations.literal: now they first broadcast their momentum—this shows they cannot do it, and it is clear.
translations.idiomatic: yet they advertise their intentions first. That proves they cannot do it, and the point is obvious.

sentences.zh: 宜及其未集，促擊蘭。

translations.literal: We ought, before they have gathered, to press the attack on Lan.
translations.idiomatic: We should strike Wu Lan before their forces can assemble.

sentences.zh: 蘭破，飛自走矣。

translations.literal: When Lan is broken, Fei will flee of himself.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wu Lan is defeated, Zhang Fei will withdraw on his own.

sentences.zh: 」洪從之，進，擊破蘭，斬之。

translations.literal: " Hong followed this, advanced, attacked and broke Lan, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: " Cao Hong followed his advice, advanced, defeated Wu Lan, and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 三月，張飛、馬超走。

translations.literal: Third month, Zhang Fei and Ma Chao fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Zhang Fei and Ma Chao withdrew.

sentences.zh: 休，魏王族子也。

translations.literal: Xiu was a clansman of the King of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xiu was a kinsman of the King of Wei.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，代郡、上谷烏桓無臣氐等反。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, the Wuhuan of Dai and Shanggu, Wuchendi and others, rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, during the fourth month, the Wuhuan of Dai and Shanggu under Wuchendi and others rebelled.

sentences.zh: 先是，魏王操召代郡太守裴潛為丞相理曹掾，操美潛治代之功，潛曰：「潛於百姓雖寬，於諸胡為峻。

translations.literal: Earlier, King Cao summoned Dai Commandery Administrator Pei Qian to be Registrar of the Chancellor's Bureau of Reasoning. Cao praised Qian's achievements in governing Dai. Qian said: "Qian, toward the common people, was lenient; toward the various Hu, stern.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, King Cao had summoned Dai Commandery Administrator Pei Qian to serve as Registrar of the Chancellor's Bureau of Reasoning. When Cao praised Qian's achievements in governing Dai, Qian said, "I was lenient toward the common people but stern toward the various Hu tribes.

sentences.zh: 今繼者必以潛為治過嚴而事加寬惠。

translations.literal: Now the successor will surely take Qian's governance as overly severe and act with added leniency and favor.
translations.idiomatic: My successor will surely judge my rule too severe and try to be more lenient and generous.

sentences.zh: 彼素驕恣，過寬必弛；

translations.literal: They by nature are arrogant and willful; if too lenient, they will surely grow lax;
translations.idiomatic: They are arrogant by nature; excessive leniency will make them lax;

sentences.zh: 既弛，又將攝之以法，此怨叛所由生也。

translations.literal: once lax, one will again restrain them with law—this is where resentment and rebellion arise.
translations.idiomatic: and once they grow lax, the new ruler will try to restrain them again with the law. That is how resentment and rebellion are born.

sentences.zh: 以勢料之，代必復叛。

translations.literal: Judging by the trend, Dai will surely rebel again.
translations.idiomatic: Judging by how matters stand, Dai will surely rebel again.

sentences.zh: 」於是操深悔還潛之速。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Cao deeply regretted having recalled Qian so quickly.
translations.idiomatic: " Cao deeply regretted having recalled Qian so soon.

sentences.zh: 後數十日，三單于反問果至。

translations.literal: Several tens of days later, reports of rebellion from the three Chanyus indeed arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Several tens of days later, reports of rebellion from the three Chanyus arrived, just as he had predicted.

sentences.zh: 操以其子鄢陵侯彰行驍騎將軍，使討之。

translations.literal: Cao made his son Marquis of Yanling Zhang act as Valiant Cavalry General and sent him to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Cao appointed his son, Marquis of Yanling Cao Zhang, acting Valiant Cavalry General, and sent him to suppress the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 彰少善射御，膂力過人。

translations.literal: Zhang from youth excelled at archery and charioteering; his physical strength surpassed other men.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Zhang excelled at archery and horsemanship, and his physical strength surpassed ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 操戒彰曰：「居家為父子，受事為君臣，動以王法從事，爾其戒之！

translations.literal: Cao admonished Zhang, saying: "At home you are father and son; in receiving affairs you are ruler and minister. In action follow the royal law in your conduct—you must be warned!
translations.idiomatic: Cao admonished Zhang, saying, "At home we are father and son, but in service we are ruler and minister. In action you must follow the royal law in all you do. Take heed!

sentences.zh: 劉備屯陽平關，夏侯淵、張郃、徐晃等與之相拒。

translations.literal: Liu Bei was encamped at Yangping Pass; Xiahou Yuan, Zhang He, Xu Huang, and others opposed him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei encamped at Yangping Pass, where Xiahou Yuan, Zhang He, Xu Huang, and others held him at bay.

sentences.zh: 備遣其將陳式等絕馬鳴閣道，徐晃擊破之。

translations.literal: Bei sent his generals Chen Shi and others to cut the Maming Pavilion road; Xu Huang attacked and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei sent his generals Chen Shi and others to sever the Maming Pavilion road, but Xu Huang attacked and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 張郃屯廣石，備攻之不能克，急書發益州兵。

translations.literal: Zhang He was garrisoned at Guangshi. Bei attacked but could not overcome him and urgently wrote to mobilize Yizhou troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang He held Guangshi, and though Liu Bei attacked he could not take it. He urgently wrote to mobilize troops from Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 諸葛亮以問從事犍為楊洪，洪曰：「漢中，益州咽喉，存亡之機會，若無漢中，則無蜀矣。

translations.literal: Zhuge Liang asked Attendant Yang Hong of Jianwei. Hong said: "Hanzhong is the throat of Yizhou, the pivot of survival and destruction. Without Hanzhong, there is no Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang consulted Attendant Yang Hong of Jianwei. Hong said, "Hanzhong is the throat of Yizhou, the pivot on which survival or destruction turns. Without Hanzhong, there is no Shu.

sentences.zh: 此家門之禍也，發兵何疑！

translations.literal: This is a calamity for our household—why hesitate to send troops!
translations.idiomatic: This is a calamity for our own house. Why hesitate to send troops!

sentences.zh: 」時法正從備北行，亮於是表洪領蜀郡太守；

translations.literal: " At this time Fa Zheng was accompanying Bei north; Liang thereupon memorialized that Hong should lead Shu Commandery as Administrator;
translations.idiomatic: " Fa Zheng was then accompanying Liu Bei north, so Zhuge Liang memorialized that Hong should serve as Administrator of Shu Commandery;

sentences.zh: 眾事皆辦，遂使即真。

translations.literal: all affairs were handled, and he was then made to assume the actual post.
translations.idiomatic: all affairs were handled, and Hong was confirmed in the post.

sentences.zh: 初，犍為太守李嚴辟洪為功曹，嚴未去犍為而洪已為蜀郡；

translations.literal: Initially, Jianwei Administrator Li Yan had recruited Hong as Merit Officer; Yan had not yet left Jianwei when Hong was already in Shu Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Jianwei Administrator Li Yan had recruited Hong as Merit Officer; Yan had not yet left Jianwei when Hong was already Administrator of Shu Commandery;

sentences.zh: 洪舉門下書佐何祗有才策，洪尚在蜀郡，而祗已為廣漢太守。

translations.literal: Hong recommended his subordinate clerk He Zhi as possessing talent and strategy; Hong was still in Shu Commandery while Zhi was already Guanghan Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Hong recommended his clerk He Zhi for talent and ability; Hong was still in Shu Commandery while Zhi had already become Administrator of Guanghan.

sentences.zh: 是以西土鹹服諸葛亮能盡時人之器用也。

translations.literal: Therefore the western lands all submitted in admiration that Zhuge Liang could fully employ the talents of men of the time.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason the western lands all admired Zhuge Liang's ability to make full use of the talents of his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，魏王操自將擊劉備；

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, King Cao of Wei personally led troops to attack Liu Bei;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, during the seventh month, King Cao personally led troops against Liu Bei;

sentences.zh: 九月，至長安。

translations.literal: ninth month, he reached Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: and in the ninth month he reached Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 曹彰擊代郡烏桓，身自搏戰，鎧中數箭，意氣益厲；

translations.literal: Cao Zhang attacked the Wuhuan of Dai Commandery, personally joining the melee; several arrows struck his armor, yet his fighting spirit grew fiercer;
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhang attacked the Wuhuan of Dai Commandery, fighting hand to hand himself. Several arrows struck his armor, yet his fighting spirit only grew fiercer;

sentences.zh: 乘勝逐北，至桑干之北，大破之，斬首、獲生以千數。

translations.literal: riding victory in pursuit north, he reached north of the Sanggan, inflicted a great defeat, and beheaded and captured alive by the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued the fleeing enemy north to beyond the Sanggan River, inflicted a crushing defeat, and took thousands of heads and captives.

sentences.zh: 時鮮卑大人軻比能將數萬騎觀望強弱，見彰力戰，所向皆破，乃請服，北方悉平。

translations.literal: At this time the Xianbei great chief Kebineng led several tens of thousands of horsemen to watch the balance of strength. Seeing Zhang fight fiercely and break all before him, he then requested submission, and the north was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the Xianbei chief Kebineng led tens of thousands of horsemen to watch which side was stronger. Seeing Zhang fight fiercely and break all before him, Kebineng submitted, and the north was fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 南陽吏民苦繇役，冬，十月，宛守將侯音反。

translations.literal: The officials and people of Nanyang suffered under corvée labor. Winter, tenth month, Wan garrison general Hou Yin rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The officials and people of Nanyang were ground down by corvée labor. In winter, during the tenth month, Wan garrison general Hou Yin rebelled.

sentences.zh: 南陽太守東裡袞與功曹應余迸竄得出；

translations.literal: Nanyang Administrator Dongli Gun and Merit Officer Ying Yu burst out and fled, escaping;
translations.idiomatic: Nanyang Administrator Dongli Gun and Merit Officer Ying Yu burst out of the city and escaped;

sentences.zh: 音遣騎追之，飛矢交流，余以身蔽袞，被七創而死，音騎執袞以歸。

translations.literal: Yin sent horsemen in pursuit; flying arrows crossed back and forth. Yu shielded Gun with his body, received seven wounds, and died; Yin's horsemen seized Gun and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yin sent horsemen in pursuit. As arrows flew thick, Yu shielded Gun with his own body, took seven wounds, and died. Yin's horsemen then seized Gun and brought him back.

sentences.zh: 時征南將軍曹仁屯樊以鎮荊州，魏王操命仁還討音。

translations.literal: At this time Campaigning South General Cao Ren was garrisoned at Fan to secure Jingzhou. King Cao of Wei ordered Ren to return and attack Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning South General Cao Ren was then garrisoned at Fan to secure Jingzhou. King Cao ordered him to return and suppress Hou Yin.

sentences.zh: 功曹宗子卿說音曰：「足下順民心，舉大事，遠近莫不望風；

translations.literal: Merit Officer Zong Ziqing urged Yin, saying: "Your Excellency follows the people's hearts and raises a great enterprise—near and far all look to your wind;
translations.idiomatic: Merit Officer Zong Ziqing urged Hou Yin, saying, "You follow the people's will and have raised a great enterprise. Near and far, all look to you with hope;

sentences.zh: 然執郡將，逆而無益，何不遣之！

translations.literal: yet holding the commandery chief is contrary and without benefit—why not release him!
translations.idiomatic: yet holding the commandery chief is contrary and gains you nothing. Why not release him!

sentences.zh: 」音從之。

translations.literal: " Yin followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " Hou Yin followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 子卿因夜逾城從太守收餘民圍音，會曹仁軍至，共攻之。

translations.literal: Ziqing by night crossed the wall, followed the Administrator, gathered the remaining people, and besieged Yin. When Cao Ren's army arrived, they attacked together.
translations.idiomatic: Ziqing crossed the wall by night, rejoined the Administrator, gathered the remaining townspeople, and besieged Hou Yin. When Cao Ren's army arrived, they attacked together.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，曹仁屠宛，斬侯音，復屯樊。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, Cao Ren slaughtered Wan, beheaded Hou Yin, and again garrisoned Fan.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, during the first month, Cao Ren sacked Wan, beheaded Hou Yin, and returned to garrison Fan.

sentences.zh: 初，夏侯淵戰雖數勝，魏王操常戒之曰：「為將當有怯弱時，不可但恃勇也。

translations.literal: Initially, though Xiahou Yuan won battle after battle, King Cao of Wei often warned him, saying: "As a general one should have times of timidity and weakness; one cannot rely on courage alone.
translations.idiomatic: Although Xiahou Yuan had won battle after battle, King Cao often warned him, saying, "A general must know moments of caution and restraint. He cannot rely on courage alone.

sentences.zh: 將當以勇為本，行之以智計；

translations.literal: A general should take courage as the root and carry it out with stratagem;
translations.idiomatic: Courage should be his foundation, but he must carry it out with strategy;

sentences.zh: 但知任勇，一匹夫敵耳。

translations.literal: if one only knows to trust courage, one is but a match for a single man.
translations.idiomatic: if he knows only how to trust courage, he is no better than a common brawler.

sentences.zh: 」及淵與劉備相拒逾年，備自陽平南渡沔水，緣山稍前，營於定軍山。

translations.literal: " When Yuan had opposed Liu Bei for more than a year, Bei from Yangping crossed the Mian River southward, followed the mountains gradually forward, and encamped at Mount Dingjun.
translations.idiomatic: " After Yuan had faced Liu Bei for more than a year, Bei crossed the Mian River south from Yangping, advanced along the mountain ridges, and encamped on Mount Dingjun.

sentences.zh: 淵引兵爭之。

translations.literal: Yuan led troops to contest it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Yuan led troops to contest the position.

sentences.zh: 法正曰：「可擊矣。

translations.literal: Fa Zheng said: "They can be attacked.
translations.idiomatic: Fa Zheng said, "They can be attacked now.

sentences.zh: 」備使討虜將軍黃忠乘高鼓噪攻之，淵軍大敗，斬淵及益州刺史趙顒。

translations.literal: " Bei sent General Who Punishes the Barbarians Huang Zhong to take the high ground, beat drums, and shout as he attacked; Yuan's army was greatly defeated, and Yuan and Yizhou Inspector Zhao Yong were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Bei sent General Who Punishes the Barbarians Huang Zhong to take the high ground, beat drums, and charge. Xiahou Yuan's army was routed, and Yuan and Yizhou Inspector Zhao Yong were slain.

sentences.zh: 張郃引兵還陽平。

translations.literal: Zhang He led his troops back to Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang He withdrew his troops to Yangping.

sentences.zh: 是時新失元帥，軍中擾擾，不知所為。

translations.literal: At this time they had newly lost their commander-in-chief; the army was in turmoil and did not know what to do.
translations.idiomatic: The army had just lost its commander-in-chief and was in turmoil, not knowing what to do.

sentences.zh: 督軍杜襲與淵司馬太原郭淮收斂散卒，號令諸軍曰：「張將軍國家名將，劉備所憚。

translations.literal: Supervising Army Officer Du Xi and Yuan's Major Taiyuan Guo Huai gathered the scattered soldiers and proclaimed to the armies: "General Zhang is a famed general of the state, whom Liu Bei fears.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Army Officer Du Xi and Yuan's Major Guo Huai of Taiyuan gathered the scattered troops and proclaimed to the armies, "General Zhang is a famed general of the state, and Liu Bei fears him.

sentences.zh: 今日事急，非張將軍不能安也。

translations.literal: Today affairs are urgent—without General Zhang there can be no stability.
translations.idiomatic: Today the situation is desperate. Without General Zhang there can be no stability.

sentences.zh: 」遂權宜推郃為軍主。

translations.literal: " They thereupon provisionally pushed He forward as army commander.
translations.idiomatic: " They thereupon provisionally made Zhang He commander of the army.

sentences.zh: 郃出，勒兵按陳，諸將皆受郃節度，眾心乃定。

translations.literal: He came forth, arrayed the troops and set the formations; all generals received He's command, and the host's hearts were then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang He came forth, arrayed the troops in formation, and all the generals accepted his command. The army's morale was restored.

sentences.zh: 明日，備欲渡漢水來攻；

translations.literal: The next day, Bei wished to cross the Han River to attack;
translations.idiomatic: The next day Liu Bei prepared to cross the Han River and attack;

sentences.zh: 諸將以眾寡不敵，欲依水為陳以拒之。

translations.literal: the generals, because their numbers were too few to match the enemy, wished to array formations along the water to resist.
translations.idiomatic: but the generals, judging their numbers too few to match the enemy, wished to form battle lines along the river to resist him.

sentences.zh: 郭淮曰：「此示弱而不足挫敵，非算也。

translations.literal: Guo Huai said: "This shows weakness and is insufficient to break the enemy's spirit—not a stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Huai said, "That shows weakness and will not break the enemy's spirit. It is no stratagem.

sentences.zh: 不如遠水為陳，引而致之，半濟而後擊之，備可破也。

translations.literal: Better to array formations far from the water, draw them in and bring them near, then strike after they are half across—Bei can be broken.
translations.idiomatic: Better to form our lines well back from the river, lure them across, and strike when they are half over. Then Liu Bei can be defeated.

sentences.zh: 」既陳，備疑，不渡。

translations.literal: " Once the formations were set, Bei grew suspicious and did not cross.
translations.idiomatic: " Once the formations were set, Liu Bei grew suspicious and did not cross.

sentences.zh: 淮遂堅守，示無還心。

translations.literal: Huai thereupon held firm defense, showing no intent to return.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Huai then held firm and showed no intention of withdrawing.

sentences.zh: 以狀聞於魏王操，操善之，遣使假郃節，復以淮為司馬。

translations.literal: They reported the situation to King Cao of Wei. Cao approved, sent envoys to grant He temporary credentials of authority, and again made Huai Major.
translations.idiomatic: They reported this to King Cao, who approved. He sent envoys to grant Zhang He temporary command authority and reappointed Guo Huai as Major.

sentences.zh: 二月，壬子晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: Second month, on the last day renzi, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the last day of the cycle, renzi, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 三月，魏王操自長安出斜谷，軍遮要以臨漢中。

translations.literal: Third month, King Cao of Wei from Chang'an exited Xie Valley, his army taking the strategic passes to approach Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, King Cao left Chang'an through Xie Valley and marched his army along the strategic passes toward Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 劉備曰：「曹公雖來，無能為也，我必有漢川矣。

translations.literal: Liu Bei said: "Though Duke Cao comes, he can do nothing—I am sure to have the Han River region.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei said, "Though Duke Cao comes, he can accomplish nothing. I am certain to hold the Han River region.

sentences.zh: 」乃斂眾拒險，終不交鋒。

translations.literal: " He then gathered his forces to hold the defiles and in the end never joined battle.
translations.idiomatic: " He gathered his forces to hold the defiles and in the end never offered battle.

sentences.zh: 操運米北山下，黃忠引兵欲取之，過期不還。

translations.literal: Cao transported grain below the northern mountains. Huang Zhong led troops wishing to seize it and, past the deadline, had not returned.
translations.idiomatic: Cao transported grain to the foot of the northern mountains. Huang Zhong led troops to seize it but failed to return by the appointed time.

sentences.zh: 翊軍將軍趙雲將數十騎出營視之，值操揚兵大出，雲猝與相遇，遂前突其陳，且鬥且卻。

translations.literal: Assisting Army General Zhao Yun with several tens of horsemen left camp to observe. He encountered Cao raising his banners and marching out in force; Yun suddenly met them, then charged their formation, fighting as he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Assisting Army General Zhao Yun rode out with several dozen horsemen to investigate. He ran into Cao Cao marching out in force, charged straight into the enemy lines, and fought his way back step by step.

sentences.zh: 魏兵散而復合，追至營下，雲入營，更大開門，偃旗息鼓。

translations.literal: Wei troops scattered and re-formed, pursuing to below the camp. Yun entered camp, again threw wide the gates, lowered the banners, and silenced the drums.
translations.idiomatic: Wei troops scattered and re-formed, pursuing him to his camp. Zhao Yun entered, threw the gates wide open, lowered the banners, and silenced the drums.

sentences.zh: 魏兵疑雲有伏，引去；

translations.literal: Wei troops suspected Yun had an ambush and withdrew;
translations.idiomatic: The Wei troops suspected an ambush and withdrew;

sentences.zh: 雲雷鼓震天，惟以勁弩於後射魏兵。

translations.literal: Yun thundered the drums to shake heaven and with powerful crossbows from the rear shot the Wei troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yun then thundered the drums to shake the heavens and raked the retreating Wei troops with powerful crossbows from the rear.

sentences.zh: 魏兵驚駭，自相蹂踐，墮漢水中死者甚多。

translations.literal: Wei troops were startled and terrified, trampling one another; many fell into the Han River and died.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei troops panicked, trampled one another, and many fell into the Han River and drowned.

sentences.zh: 備明旦自來，至雲營，視昨戰處，曰：「子龍一身都為膽也！

translations.literal: The next morning Bei came in person to Yun's camp, viewed yesterday's battlefield, and said: "Zilong's whole body is courage!
translations.idiomatic: The next morning Liu Bei came in person to Zhao Yun's camp, surveyed yesterday's battlefield, and said, "Zilong's whole body is courage!

sentences.zh: 」操與備相守積月，魏軍士多亡。

translations.literal: " Cao and Bei faced each other for months; many Wei soldiers deserted.
translations.idiomatic: " Cao and Liu Bei faced each other for months, and many Wei soldiers deserted.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，操悉引出漢中諸軍還長安，劉備遂有漢中。

translations.literal: Summer, fifth month, Cao drew out all the Hanzhong armies and returned to Chang'an; Liu Bei thereupon possessed Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, during the fifth month, Cao withdrew all his Hanzhong armies to Chang'an, and Liu Bei thereby secured Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 操恐劉備北取武都氐以逼關中，問雍州刺史張既，既曰：「可勸使北出就谷以避賊，前至者厚其寵賞，則先者知利，後必慕之。

translations.literal: Cao feared Liu Bei would take Wudu Di in the north to press on Guanzhong and asked Yongzhou Inspector Zhang Ji. Ji said: "They can be urged to move north to seek grain and avoid the bandits. Those who arrive first should receive rich favor and rewards; then those ahead will know the profit, and those behind will surely emulate them.
translations.idiomatic: Cao feared Liu Bei would seize the Di of Wudu in the north and press on Guanzhong, and asked Yongzhou Inspector Zhang Ji. Ji said, "Urge them to move north to seek grain and escape the enemy. Reward those who arrive first generously, so the first will see the benefit and the rest will follow.

sentences.zh: 」操從之，使既之武都，徙氐五萬餘落出居扶風、天水界。

translations.literal: " Cao followed this, sent Ji to Wudu, and moved more than fifty thousand Di households out to dwell on the borders of Fufeng and Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: " Cao followed his advice, sent Ji to Wudu, and relocated more than fifty thousand Di households to the borders of Fufeng and Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 武威顏俊、張掖和鸞、酒泉黃華、西平麴演等，各據其郡，自號將軍，更相攻擊。

translations.literal: Yan Jun of Wuwei, He Luan of Zhangye, Huang Hua of Jiuquan, Qu Yan of Xiping, and others each held their commanderies, styled themselves generals, and attacked one another in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Jun of Wuwei, He Luan of Zhangye, Huang Hua of Jiuquan, Qu Yan of Xiping, and others each held their commanderies, styled themselves generals, and attacked one another in turn.

sentences.zh: 俊遣使送母及子詣魏王操為質以求助。

translations.literal: Jun sent envoys to deliver his mother and sons to King Cao of Wei as hostages to seek aid.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Jun sent envoys to deliver his mother and sons to King Cao as hostages in seeking aid.

sentences.zh: 操問張既，既曰：「俊等外假國威，內生傲悖，計定勢足，後即反耳。

translations.literal: Cao asked Zhang Ji. Ji said: "Jun and the others outwardly borrow the state's authority while inwardly breeding arrogance and rebellion. Once their plans are settled and their power sufficient, afterward they will turn against you.
translations.idiomatic: Cao asked Zhang Ji. Ji said, "Jun and the others borrow the state's authority outwardly while breeding arrogance and rebellion within. Once their plans are settled and their power secure, they will turn against you.

sentences.zh: 今方事定蜀，且宜兩存而斗之，猶卞莊子之刺虎，坐收其敝也。

translations.literal: Now we are just settling affairs in Shu; for the moment it is fitting to let both sides exist and have them fight, like Bian Zhuangzi stabbing the tiger—sitting to collect their exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: We are just now settling affairs in Shu. For the moment, let both sides survive and fight each other, like Bian Zhuangzi stabbing the tiger while it fights—then sit back and collect the spoils when they are exhausted.

sentences.zh: 」王曰：「善！

translations.literal: " The King said: "Good!
translations.idiomatic: " The King said, "Excellent!

sentences.zh: 」歲餘，鸞遂殺俊，武威王祕又殺鸞。

translations.literal: " After more than a year, Luan then killed Jun, and Wang Mi of Wuwei again killed Luan.
translations.idiomatic: " More than a year later, He Luan killed Yan Jun, and Wang Mi of Wuwei then killed He Luan.

sentences.zh: 劉備遣宜都太守扶風孟達從秭歸北攻房陵，殺房陵太守蒯祺。

translations.literal: Liu Bei sent Yidu Administrator Meng Da of Fufeng from Zigui north to attack Fangling and killed Fangling Administrator Kuai Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei sent Yidu Administrator Meng Da of Fufeng from Zigui north to attack Fangling and killed its administrator, Kuai Qi.

sentences.zh: 又遣養子副軍中郎將劉封自漢中乘沔水下，統達軍，與達會攻上庸，上庸太守申耽舉郡降。

translations.literal: He also sent his adopted son Deputy Army Zhonglang General Liu Feng from Hanzhong down the Mian River, commanding Da's army, joining Da to attack Shangyong; Shangyong Administrator Shen Dan raised the commandery in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent his adopted son, Deputy Army Zhonglang General Liu Feng, from Hanzhong down the Mian River to take command of Meng Da's forces. Together they attacked Shangyong, and Administrator Shen Dan surrendered the entire commandery.

sentences.zh: 備加耽征北將軍，領上庸太守，以耽弟儀為建信將軍、西城太守。

translations.literal: Bei promoted Dan to Campaigning North General, retaining him as Shangyong Administrator, and made Dan's younger brother Yi Establishing Trust General and Xicheng Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei promoted Shen Dan to Campaigning North General while keeping him as Administrator of Shangyong, and appointed Dan's younger brother Shen Yi Establishing Trust General and Administrator of Xicheng.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，劉備自稱漢中王，設壇場於沔陽，陳兵列眾，群臣陪位，讀奏訖，乃拜受璽綬，御王冠。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, Liu Bei styled himself King of Han. He set up an altar at Mianyang, arrayed troops and lined the host, with ministers and officials in attendance. When the memorial was read to its end, he bowed to receive the seal and sash and donned the king's crown.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, during the seventh month, Liu Bei styled himself King of Han. At Mianyang he set up an altar, arrayed his troops, and seated his ministers in attendance. When the memorial had been read, he bowed to receive the seal and sash and placed the king's crown upon his head.

sentences.zh: 因驛拜章，上還所假左將軍、宜城亭侯印綬。

translations.literal: By post he submitted a memorial, returning upward the borrowed seal and sash of Left General and Marquis of Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: By courier he submitted a memorial returning the seal and sash of Left General and Marquis of Yicheng that had been lent him.

sentences.zh: 立子禪為王太子。

translations.literal: He established his son Shan as royal heir.
translations.idiomatic: He named his son Liu Shan royal heir.

sentences.zh: 拔牙門將軍義陽魏延為鎮遠將軍，領漢中太守，以鎮漢川。

translations.literal: He removed General of the Rapid Gate Wei Yan of Yiyang and made him Pacifying the Distance General, leading Hanzhong Administrator, to secure the Han River region.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted General of the Rapid Gate Wei Yan of Yiyang to Pacifying the Distance General and Administrator of Hanzhong to secure the Han River region.

sentences.zh: 備還治成都，以許靖為太傅，法正為尚書令，關羽為前將軍，張飛為右將軍，馬超為左將軍，黃忠為後將軍，餘皆進位有差。

translations.literal: Bei returned to administer from Chengdu, making Xu Jing Grand Tutor, Fa Zheng Director of the Masters of Writing, Guan Yu Forward General, Zhang Fei Right General, Ma Chao Left General, Huang Zhong Rear General; the rest all advanced in rank with differences.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei returned to govern from Chengdu. He appointed Xu Jing Grand Tutor, Fa Zheng Director of the Masters of Writing, Guan Yu Forward General, Zhang Fei Right General, Ma Chao Left General, and Huang Zhong Rear General, while the rest were promoted in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 遣益州前部司馬犍為費詩即授關羽印授，羽聞黃忠位與己並，怒曰：「大丈夫終不與老兵同列！

translations.literal: He sent Yizhou Forward Department Major Fei Shi of Jianwei to confer Guan Yu's seal and credentials at once. Yu, hearing that Huang Zhong's rank was equal to his own, angrily said: "A great man will never stand in the same rank as an old soldier!
translations.idiomatic: He sent Yizhou Forward Department Major Fei Shi of Jianwei to confer Guan Yu's seal and credentials. When Yu learned that Huang Zhong's rank equaled his own, he angrily declared, "A great man will never stand in the same rank as an old soldier!

sentences.zh: 」不肯受拜。

translations.literal: " He refused to accept the appointment and bow.
translations.idiomatic: " He refused to accept the appointment.

sentences.zh: 詩謂羽曰：「夫立王業者，所用非一。

translations.literal: Shi said to Yu: "In establishing a royal enterprise, those employed are not one kind.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Shi said to Guan Yu, "In establishing a royal enterprise, one employs many kinds of men.

sentences.zh: 昔蕭、曹與高祖少小親舊，而陳、韓亡命後至；

translations.literal: In former times Xiao and Cao were the High Ancestor's childhood intimates, while Chen and Han were fugitives who came later;
translations.idiomatic: In former times Xiao He and Cao Shen were the High Ancestor's childhood intimates, while Chen Ping and Han Xin were fugitives who came later;

sentences.zh: 論其班列，韓最居上，未聞蕭、曹以此為怨。

translations.literal: judging their order of rank, Han stood highest, yet one never heard that Xiao and Cao resented this.
translations.idiomatic: yet in order of rank Han Xin stood highest, and one never heard that Xiao He or Cao Shen resented it.

sentences.zh: 今漢中王以一時之功隆崇漢室；

translations.literal: Now the King of Han, by merit of the moment, has exalted and honored the House of Han;
translations.idiomatic: Now the King of Han, by merit won in this moment, has exalted the House of Han;

sentences.zh: 然意之輕重，寧當與君侯齊乎！

translations.literal: yet in intent and weight, how could he be your equal!
translations.idiomatic: yet in intent and weight, how could he be your equal!

sentences.zh: 且王與君侯譬猶一體，同休等戚，禍福共之。

translations.literal: Moreover the King and Your Lordship are like one body, sharing fortune and misfortune alike, blessings and calamities together.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the King and Your Lordship are like one body, sharing fortune and misfortune, blessing and calamity alike.

sentences.zh: 愚謂君侯不宜計官號之高下、爵祿之多少為意也。

translations.literal: I foolishly think Your Lordship ought not to take as your concern the high or low of titles or the more or less of rank and salary.
translations.idiomatic: I think Your Lordship ought not to concern yourself with the high or low of titles or the size of rank and salary.

sentences.zh: 僕一介之使，銜命之人，君侯不受拜，如是便還，但相為惜此舉動，恐有後悔耳。

translations.literal: I am but a single envoy, one who bears command. If Your Lordship will not accept the appointment and bow, I shall return thus—but I grieve for you over this action, fearing there may be regret later.
translations.idiomatic: I am but a single envoy bearing the King's command. If Your Lordship will not accept, I must return as I came—but I grieve for you over this action, fearing you may regret it later.

sentences.zh: 」羽大感悟，遽即受拜。

translations.literal: " Yu was greatly moved to understanding and at once accepted the appointment and bowed.
translations.idiomatic: " Guan Yu was deeply moved and at once accepted the appointment.

sentences.zh: 詔以魏王操夫人卞氏為王后。

translations.literal: An edict made Lady Bian, wife of King Cao of Wei, queen.
translations.idiomatic: An edict named Lady Bian, wife of King Cao, queen.

sentences.zh: 孫權攻合肥。

translations.literal: Sun Quan attacked Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan attacked Hefei.

sentences.zh: 時諸州兵戍淮南。

translations.literal: At the time the troops of the various provinces garrisoned Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, troops from the various provinces were garrisoned in Huainan.

sentences.zh: 揚州刺史溫恢謂兗州刺史裴潛曰：「此間雖有賊，然不足憂。

translations.literal: Yang Province Inspector Wen Hui said to Yan Province Inspector Pei Qian: "Though there are bandits in this region, yet they are not enough to worry about.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Hui, Inspector of Yang Province, said to Pei Qian, Inspector of Yan Province, "Though there are bandits here, they are not worth worrying about.

sentences.zh: 今水潦方生，而子孝縣軍，無有遠備，關羽驍猾，正恐征南有變耳。

translations.literal: Now floodwaters are just arising, yet Zixiao has left his army exposed, with no distant preparations; Guan Yu is fierce and cunning—what I truly fear is that there may be trouble on the southern expedition front."
translations.idiomatic: Floods are just beginning, yet Zixiao has exposed his army with no distant preparations; Guan Yu is fierce and cunning—I truly fear there may be trouble on the southern front."

sentences.zh: 」已而關羽果使南郡太守糜芳守江陵，將軍傅士仁守公安，羽自率眾攻曹仁於樊。

translations.literal: Before long Guan Yu indeed had Nan Commandery Administrator Mi Fang guard Jiangling and General Fu Shiren guard Gong'an; Yu himself led the host to attack Cao Ren at Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Guan Yu indeed had Nan Commandery Administrator Mi Fang guard Jiangling and General Fu Shiren guard Gong'an; Guan Yu himself led his forces to attack Cao Ren at Fan.

sentences.zh: 仁使左將軍-{于}-禁、立義將軍龐德等屯樊北。

translations.literal: Ren sent Left General Yu Jin, General Who Establishes Righteousness Pang De, and others to encamp north of Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Ren sent Left General Yu Jin, General Who Establishes Righteousness Pang De, and others to encamp north of Fan.

sentences.zh: 八月，大霖雨，漢水溢，平地數丈，-{于}-禁等七軍皆沒。

translations.literal: Eighth month, great torrential rains; the Han River overflowed, and on level ground the water stood several zhang deep; Yu Jin and the seven armies were all submerged.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, torrential rains fell; the Han River overflowed until the water stood several zhang deep on level ground, and Yu Jin's seven armies were drowned.

sentences.zh: 禁與諸將登高避水，羽乘大船就攻之，禁等窮迫，遂降。

translations.literal: Jin and the generals climbed high to escape the water; Yu took large boats to attack them; Jin and the others were driven to extremity and thereupon surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jin and the other generals climbed high ground to escape the flood; Guan Yu sailed large boats to attack them; hard pressed, Yu Jin and his men surrendered.

sentences.zh: 龐德在堤上，被甲持弓，箭不虛發，自平旦力戰，至日過中，羽攻益急；

translations.literal: Pang De was on the dike, armored and holding a bow; not an arrow was wasted; from early dawn he fought with all his strength until the sun passed midday; Yu's attacks grew ever fiercer;
translations.idiomatic: Pang De stood on the embankment in armor with bow in hand; every arrow found its mark; from early dawn he fought with all his strength until past midday, while Guan Yu's assaults grew ever fiercer;

sentences.zh: 矢盡，短兵接，德戰益怒，氣愈壯，而水浸盛，吏士盡降。

translations.literal: When the arrows were exhausted, close combat ensued; De fought ever angrier, his courage ever bolder, but the flood rose ever higher, and officers and soldiers all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When his arrows ran out, he closed at close quarters; Pang De fought ever angrier, his spirit ever bolder, but the flood rose ever higher and his officers and soldiers all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 德乘小船欲還仁營，水盛船覆，失弓矢，獨抱船覆水中，為羽所得，立而不跪。

translations.literal: De took a small boat intending to return to Ren's camp; the water was high and the boat capsized; he lost bow and arrows; alone clinging to the overturned boat in the water, he was captured by Yu; he stood and would not kneel.
translations.idiomatic: Pang De took a small boat intending to return to Cao Ren's camp; the flood was high and the boat capsized; he lost bow and arrows and, clinging alone to the overturned hull, was captured by Guan Yu and stood without kneeling.

sentences.zh: 羽謂曰：「卿兄在漢中，我欲以卿為將，不早降何為！

translations.literal: Yu said to him: "Your elder brother is in Hanzhong; I wish to make you a general—why not surrender early!"
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu said to him, "Your elder brother is in Hanzhong; I wish to make you a general—why not surrender sooner!"

sentences.zh: 」德罵羽曰：「豎子，何謂降也！

translations.literal: De cursed Yu, saying: "You whelp—what talk is this of surrender!"
translations.idiomatic: Pang De cursed Guan Yu, saying, "You whelp—what talk is this of surrender!"

sentences.zh: 魏王帶甲百萬，威振天下。

translations.literal: The King of Wei has a million armored men; his might shakes all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Wei has a million armored men, and his might shakes the realm.

sentences.zh: 汝劉備庸才耳，豈能敵邪！

translations.literal: You—Liu Bei—is but mediocre talent; how could he be a match!
translations.idiomatic: You and Liu Bei are but mediocre talents—how could you be a match!

sentences.zh: 我寧為國家鬼，不為賊將也！

translations.literal: I would rather be a ghost of the state than a general of bandits!
translations.idiomatic: I would rather be a ghost of the state than a general of bandits!

sentences.zh: 」羽殺之。

translations.literal: Yu killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu killed him.

sentences.zh: 魏王操聞之流涕曰：「吾知-{于}-禁三十年，何意臨危處難，反不及龐德邪！

translations.literal: King Cao Cao heard of it and wept, saying: "I have known Yu Jin for thirty years—who would have thought that facing peril in crisis, he would prove inferior to Pang De!"
translations.idiomatic: When King Cao Cao heard of it, he wept and said, "I have known Yu Jin for thirty years—who would have thought that facing peril in crisis, he would prove inferior to Pang De!"

sentences.zh: 」封德二子為列侯。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed De's two sons as marquises of a column.
translations.idiomatic: He enfeoffed Pang De's two sons as full marquises.

sentences.zh: 羽急攻樊城，城得水，往往崩壞，眾皆恟懼。

translations.literal: Yu pressed the attack on Fancheng; the city took on water and sections often collapsed; all were alarmed and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu pressed the attack on Fancheng; the city took on water and sections of the wall often collapsed; the garrison was alarmed and afraid.

sentences.zh: 或謂曹仁曰：「今日之危，非力所支，可及羽圍未合，乘輕船夜走。

translations.literal: Someone said to Cao Ren: "Today's peril cannot be sustained by strength; while Yu's encirclement is not yet complete, you could take light boats and flee by night."
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to Cao Ren, "Today's peril cannot be borne by strength alone; while Guan Yu's siege is not yet closed, you could take light boats and flee by night."

sentences.zh: 」汝南太守滿龐曰：「山水速疾，冀其不久。

translations.literal: Runan Administrator Man Chong said: "The mountain flood is swift—I hope it will not last long.
translations.idiomatic: Runan Administrator Man Chong said, "The mountain flood is swift—I hope it will not last long.

sentences.zh: 聞羽遣別將已在郟下，自許以南，百姓擾擾，羽所以不敢遂進者，恐吾軍掎其後耳。

translations.literal: I hear Yu has sent a separate general who is already at Xià; from Xu southward the common people are in turmoil; the reason Yu does not dare advance directly is that he fears our army will strike him from behind."
translations.idiomatic: I hear Guan Yu has sent a separate general who is already at Xià; from Xu southward the common people are in turmoil; the reason Guan Yu does not dare press forward is that he fears our army will seize him from behind."

sentences.zh: 今若遁去，洪河以南，非復國家有也，君宜待之。

translations.literal: If you flee now, south of the great river will no longer belong to the state—you ought to wait it out."
translations.idiomatic: If you flee now, south of the great river will no longer belong to the state—you should wait it out."

sentences.zh: 」仁曰：「善！

translations.literal: Ren said: "Good!"
translations.idiomatic: Cao Ren said, "Good!"

sentences.zh: 」乃沉白馬與軍人盟誓，同心固守。

translations.literal: He then sank a white horse and swore an oath with the soldiers, united in holding fast.
translations.idiomatic: He then sank a white horse and swore an oath with the soldiers to hold firm together.

sentences.zh: 城中人馬才數千人，城不沒者數板。

translations.literal: Within the city there were only a few thousand men and horses; only several boards' height of the wall was not submerged.
translations.idiomatic: Within the city there were only a few thousand men and horses; only several boards' height of the wall remained above water.

sentences.zh: 羽乘船臨城，立圍數重，外內斷絕。

translations.literal: Yu sailed boats to the city and established encirclements in several rings, cutting off inside and outside completely.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu sailed boats up to the city and established encirclements layer upon layer, cutting off the city completely inside and out.

sentences.zh: 羽又遣別將圍將軍呂常於襄陽。

translations.literal: Yu also sent a separate general to besiege General Lü Chang at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu also sent a separate general to besiege General Lü Chang at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史胡修、南鄉太守傅方皆降於羽。

translations.literal: Jing Province Inspector Hu Xiu and Nanxiang Administrator Fu Fang both surrendered to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Province Inspector Hu Xiu and Nanxiang Administrator Fu Fang both surrendered to Guan Yu.

sentences.zh: 初，沛國魏諷有惑眾才，傾動鄴都，魏相國鐘繇辟以為西曹掾。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wei Feng of Pei had a talent for swaying the masses and stirred up the capital at Ye; Wei Chancellor Zhong Yao recruited him as Western Bureau Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wei Feng of Pei had a talent for swaying the masses and stirred up the capital at Ye; Wei Chancellor Zhong Yao recruited him as Western Bureau Attendant.

sentences.zh: 滎陽任覽，與諷友善。

translations.literal: Ren Lan of Xingyang was on friendly terms with Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Lan of Xingyang was friendly with Wei Feng.

sentences.zh: 同郡鄭袤，泰之子也，每謂覽曰：「諷奸雄，終必為亂。

translations.literal: Zheng Mao of the same commandery, son of Zheng Tai, often said to Lan: "Feng is a villainous hero—in the end he will surely bring rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Mao of the same commandery, son of Zheng Tai, often said to Ren Lan, "Wei Feng is a villainous hero—he will surely bring rebellion in the end."

sentences.zh: 」九月，諷潛結徒黨，與長樂衛尉陳禕謀襲鄴；

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Feng secretly gathered partisans and with Changlean Commandant Guard Chen Yi plotted to strike Ye;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Wei Feng secretly gathered a faction and with Changlean Commandant Guard Chen Yi plotted to strike Ye;

sentences.zh: 未及期，禕懼而告之。

translations.literal: Before the appointed date, Yi was afraid and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Before the date arrived, Chen Yi was afraid and reported it.

sentences.zh: 太子丕誅諷，連坐死者數千人，鐘繇坐免官。

translations.literal: Heir Apparent Pi executed Feng; those implicated in death numbered several thousand; Zhong Yao was dismissed from office for his guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Heir Apparent Cao Pi executed Wei Feng; those implicated in death numbered several thousand; Zhong Yao was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 初，丞相主簿楊修與丁儀兄弟謀立曹植為魏嗣，五官將丕患之，以車載廢簏內朝歌長吳質，與之謀。

translations.literal: Earlier, Chancellor Chief Clerk Yang Xiu and the brothers Ding Yi plotted to establish Cao Zhi as heir of Wei; General of the Five Senses Cao Pi was troubled by this and used a cart carrying a discarded bamboo hamper to smuggle Chaoge Prefect Wu Zhi inside to plot with him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Chancellor Chief Clerk Yang Xiu and the brothers Ding Yi plotted to establish Cao Zhi as heir of Wei; General of the Five Senses Cao Pi was troubled by this and used a cart carrying a discarded bamboo hamper to smuggle Chaoge Prefect Wu Zhi inside to plot with him.

sentences.zh: 修以白魏王操，操未及推驗。

translations.literal: Xiu reported this to King Cao Cao; Cao had not yet investigated.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiu reported this to King Cao Cao; Cao Cao had not yet investigated.

sentences.zh: 丕懼，告質，質曰：「無害也。

translations.literal: Pi was afraid and told Zhi; Zhi said: "No harm."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi was afraid and told Wu Zhi; Wu Zhi said, "No harm."

sentences.zh: 」明日，復以簏載絹以入，修復白之，推驗，無人；

translations.literal: The next day he again used a hamper cart carrying silk to enter; Xiu again reported it; when they investigated, there was no one;
translations.idiomatic: The next day he again used a hamper cart carrying silk to enter; Yang Xiu again reported it; when they investigated, there was no one;

sentences.zh: 操由是疑焉。

translations.literal: Cao from this became suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao from this became suspicious.

sentences.zh: 其後植以驕縱見疏，而植故連綴修不止，修亦不敢自絕。

translations.literal: Afterward Zhi came to be estranged for arrogance and license, yet Zhi still continually associated with Xiu without ceasing, and Xiu also did not dare break off on his own.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Cao Zhi came to be estranged for arrogance and license, yet he still continually associated with Yang Xiu without ceasing, and Yang Xiu also did not dare break off on his own.

sentences.zh: 每當就植，慮事有闕，忖度操意，豫作答教十餘條，敕門下，「教出，隨所問答之」，於是教裁出，答已入；

translations.literal: Whenever he was about to visit Zhi, fearing there might be gaps in affairs, he reckoned Cao's intent and prepared model answers in advance in more than ten items, instructing those at the gate: "When the command comes out, answer according to what is asked"—and so when the command was cut and issued, the answers were already submitted;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he was about to visit Cao Zhi, fearing there might be gaps in matters, he reckoned Cao Cao's intent and prepared answers in advance in more than ten items, instructing those at the gate, "When the command comes out, answer according to what is asked"—and so when the command was issued, the answers were already submitted;

sentences.zh: 操怪其捷，推問，始洩。

translations.literal: Cao marveled at the speed; when he pressed the inquiry, it was finally revealed.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao marveled at the speed; when he pressed the inquiry, it was finally revealed.

sentences.zh: 操亦以修袁術之甥，惡之，乃發修前後漏洩言教，交關諸侯，收殺之。

translations.literal: Cao also hated Xiu as Yuan Shu's nephew; he then exposed Xiu's past leaks of private commands and communications with various lords, and had him arrested and executed.
