translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao also hated Yang Xiu as Yuan Shu's nephew; he then exposed Yang Xiu's past leaks of private commands and communications with various lords, and had him arrested and executed.

sentences.zh: 魏王操以杜襲為留府長史，駐關中。

translations.literal: King Cao Cao appointed Du Xi as Chief Clerk remaining at headquarters, stationed in Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: King Cao Cao appointed Du Xi Chief Clerk remaining at headquarters, stationed in Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 關中營帥許攸擁部曲不歸附，而有慢言，操大怒，先欲伐之。

translations.literal: Guanzhong camp commander Xu You held his personal troops without submitting, and spoke insolently; Cao was greatly angered and at first intended to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong camp commander Xu You held his personal troops without submitting and spoke insolently; Cao Cao was greatly angered and at first intended to attack him.

sentences.zh: 群臣多諫宜招懷攸，共討強敵；

translations.literal: Many ministers remonstrated that he ought to win Xu You over and together attack the strong foe;
translations.idiomatic: Many ministers remonstrated that he ought to win Xu You over and together attack the strong foe;

sentences.zh: 操橫刀於膝，作色不聽。

translations.literal: Cao placed a sword across his knees, showed anger, and would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao placed a sword across his knees, showed anger, and would not listen.

sentences.zh: 襲入欲諫，操逆謂之曰：「吾計已定，卿勿復言！

translations.literal: Xi entered intending to remonstrate; Cao preempted him, saying: "My plan is settled—you need speak no more!"
translations.idiomatic: Du Xi entered intending to remonstrate; Cao Cao preempted him, saying, "My plan is settled—you need speak no more!"

sentences.zh: 」襲曰：「若殿下計是邪，臣方助殿下成之；

translations.literal: Xi said: "If Your Highness's plan is right, then your servant is just about to help Your Highness accomplish it;
translations.idiomatic: Du Xi said, "If Your Highness's plan is right, then your servant is just about to help Your Highness accomplish it;

sentences.zh: 若殿下計非邪，雖成，宜改之。

translations.literal: if Your Highness's plan is wrong, even if accomplished, it ought to be changed.
translations.idiomatic: if Your Highness's plan is wrong, even if accomplished, it ought to be changed.

sentences.zh: 殿下逆臣令勿言，何待下之不闡乎！

translations.literal: Your Highness preempts your servant with orders not to speak—how is this treating one's subordinate without openness!"
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness preempts your servant with orders not to speak—how is this treating one's subordinate without openness!"

sentences.zh: 」操曰：「許攸慢吾，如何可置！

translations.literal: Cao said: "Xu You insults me—how can he be spared!"
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao said, "Xu You insults me—how can he be spared!"

sentences.zh: 」襲曰：「殿下謂許攸何如人邪？

translations.literal: Xi said: "What kind of man does Your Highness consider Xu You to be?"
translations.idiomatic: Du Xi said, "What kind of man does Your Highness consider Xu You to be?"

sentences.zh: 」操曰：「凡人也。

translations.literal: Cao said: "An ordinary man."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao said, "An ordinary man."

sentences.zh: 」襲曰：「夫惟賢知賢，惟聖知聖，凡人安能知非凡人邪！

translations.literal: Xi said: "Only the worthy know the worthy, only the sage knows the sage—how could an ordinary man know a non-ordinary man!"
translations.idiomatic: Du Xi said, "Only the worthy know the worthy, only the sage knows the sage—how could an ordinary man know a non-ordinary man!"

sentences.zh: 方今豺狼當路而狐狸是先，人將謂殿下避強攻弱；

translations.literal: Now wolves and leopards block the road, yet it is foxes you attack first—people will say Your Highness avoids the strong and strikes the weak;
translations.idiomatic: Now wolves and leopards block the road, yet it is foxes you attack first—people will say Your Highness avoids the strong and strikes the weak;

sentences.zh: 進不為勇，退不為仁。

translations.literal: Advancing is not courage; retreating is not benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing is not courage; retreating is not benevolence.

sentences.zh: 臣聞千鈞之弩，不為鼷鼠發機；

translations.literal: I have heard that a crossbow of a thousand jun does not release its trigger for a tiny mouse;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that a crossbow of a thousand jun does not release its trigger for a tiny mouse;

sentences.zh: 萬石之鐘，不以莛撞起音。

translations.literal: a bell of ten thousand dan does not sound from a pestle striking it.
translations.idiomatic: a bell of ten thousand dan does not sound from a pestle striking it.

sentences.zh: 今區區之許攸，何足以勞神武哉！

translations.literal: Now this petty Xu You—how is he enough to tax divine martial prowess!"
translations.idiomatic: Now this petty Xu You—how is he enough to tax divine martial prowess!"

sentences.zh: 」操曰：「善！

translations.literal: Cao said: "Good!"
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao said, "Good!"

sentences.zh: 」遂厚撫攸，攸即歸復。

translations.literal: He then treated Xu You generously; Xu You at once returned and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He then treated Xu You generously; Xu You at once returned and submitted.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，魏王操至洛陽。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month: King Cao Cao arrived at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, King Cao Cao arrived at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 陸渾民孫狼等作亂，殺縣主簿，南附關羽。

translations.literal: Sun Lang and others of Luhun raised rebellion, killed the county chief clerk, and went south to submit to Guan Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Lang and others of Luhun raised rebellion, killed the county chief clerk, and went south to submit to Guan Yu.

sentences.zh: 羽授狼印，給兵，還為寇賊，自許以南，往往遙應羽，羽威震華夏。

translations.literal: Yu gave Lang a seal, supplied troops, and sent him back as a raiding bandit; from Xu southward many often responded to Yu from afar; Yu's might shook the Central States.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu gave Sun Lang a seal, supplied troops, and sent him back as a raiding bandit; from Xu southward many often responded to Guan Yu from afar; Guan Yu's might shook the Central States.

sentences.zh: 魏王操議徙許都以避其銳，丞相軍司馬司馬懿、西曹屬蔣濟言於操曰：「-{于}-禁等為水所沒，非戰攻之失，於國家大計未足有損。

translations.literal: King Cao Cao considered moving the capital from Xu to avoid his sharp edge; Chief Clerk to the Chancellor Sima Yi and Western Bureau Subordinate Jiang Ji said to Cao: "Yu Jin and the others were submerged by water—not a failure in battle—and for the state's grand design it is not enough to count as a loss.
translations.idiomatic: King Cao Cao considered moving the capital from Xu to avoid Guan Yu's sharp edge; Chief Clerk to the Chancellor Sima Yi and Western Bureau Subordinate Jiang Ji said to Cao Cao, "Yu Jin and the others were drowned by flood—not a failure in battle—and for the state's grand design it is not enough to count as a loss.

sentences.zh: 劉備、孫權，外親內疏，關羽得志，權必不願也。

translations.literal: Liu Bei and Sun Quan are close outside but estranged within; when Guan Yu gets his way, Quan is sure not to be pleased."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei and Sun Quan are close outside but estranged within; when Guan Yu gets his way, Sun Quan is sure not to be pleased."

sentences.zh: 可遣人勸權躡其後，許割江南以封權，則樊圍自解。

translations.literal: You can send someone to urge Quan to follow in his rear, promising to cede the lands south of the Yangtze to enfeoff Quan—then the siege of Fan will resolve itself."
translations.idiomatic: You can send someone to urge Sun Quan to follow in his rear, promising to cede the lands south of the Yangtze to enfeoff him—then the siege of Fan will resolve itself."

sentences.zh: 」操從之。

translations.literal: Cao followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao followed this advice.

sentences.zh: 初，魯肅嘗勸孫權以曹操尚存，宜且撫輯關羽，與之同仇，不可失也。

translations.literal: Earlier, Lu Su had urged Sun Quan that while Cao Cao still lived, he ought for the time being to soothe and unite with Guan Yu and share the same enemy—this must not be lost.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Lu Su had urged Sun Quan that while Cao Cao still lived, he ought for the time being to soothe and unite with Guan Yu and share the same enemy—this must not be lost.

sentences.zh: 及呂蒙代肅屯陸口，以為羽素驍雄，有兼併之心，且居國上流，其勢難久，密言於權曰：「今令征虜守南郡，潘璋住白帝，蔣欽將遊兵萬人循江上下，應敵所在，蒙為國家前據襄陽，如此，何憂於操，何賴於羽！

translations.literal: When Lü Meng replaced Su garrisoning Lukou, he thought Yu had always been fierce and heroic, with a mind to annex territory, and moreover held the upstream of the state—the situation could not last long; he spoke secretly to Quan, saying: "Now order the General Who Pacifies Barbarians to guard Nan Commandery, Pan Zhang to hold White Emperor, Jiang Qin to lead ten thousand mobile troops up and down the river responding wherever the enemy appears; Meng himself will advance for the state and hold Xiangyang beforehand—thus, why worry about Cao Cao, why rely on Guan Yu!
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Meng replaced Lu Su garrisoning Lukou, he thought Guan Yu had always been fierce and heroic, with a mind to annex territory, and moreover held the upstream of the state—the situation could not last long; he spoke secretly to Sun Quan, saying, "Now order the General Who Pacifies Barbarians to guard Nan Commandery, Pan Zhang to hold White Emperor, Jiang Qin to lead ten thousand mobile troops up and down the river responding wherever the enemy appears; I myself will advance for the state and hold Xiangyang beforehand—thus, why worry about Cao Cao, why rely on Guan Yu!

sentences.zh: 且羽君臣矜其詐力，所在反覆，不可以腹心待也。

translations.literal: Moreover Yu and his lord and ministers pride themselves on their cunning strength; wherever they go they turn back and forth—they cannot be treated with innermost trust."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Guan Yu and his lord and ministers pride themselves on their cunning strength; wherever they go they turn back and forth—they cannot be treated with innermost trust."

sentences.zh: 今羽所以未便東向者，以至尊聖明，蒙等尚存也。

translations.literal: The reason Yu has not yet turned east is that Your Majesty is sage and enlightened and Meng and the others still live."
translations.idiomatic: The reason Guan Yu has not yet turned east is that Your Majesty is sage and enlightened and Lü Meng and the others still live."

sentences.zh: 今不於強壯時圖之，一旦僵仆，欲復陳力，其可得邪！

translations.literal: If you do not plot against him while he is still strong, once he stiffens and falls, wanting again to deploy your strength—how could that be obtained!"
translations.idiomatic: If you do not plot against him while he is still strong, once he stiffens and falls, wanting again to deploy your strength—how could that be obtained!"

sentences.zh: 」權曰：「今欲先取徐州，然後取羽，何如？

translations.literal: Quan said: "I wish first to take Xuzhou, then take Yu—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan said, "I wish first to take Xuzhou, then take Guan Yu—what do you think?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「今操遠在河北，撫集幽、冀，未暇東顧，徐土守兵，聞不足言，往自可克。

translations.literal: He replied: "Now Cao Cao is far away in Hebei, soothing and gathering You and Ji, with no leisure to look east; the garrison troops of Xu are not worth mentioning—to go is to take it at once.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Now Cao Cao is far away in Hebei, soothing and gathering You and Ji, with no leisure to look east; the garrison troops of Xu are not worth mentioning—to go is to take it at once.

sentences.zh: 然地勢陸通，驍騎所騁，至尊今日取徐州，操後旬必來爭，雖以七八萬人守之，猶當懷憂。

translations.literal: Yet the terrain is open land where swift cavalry can run free; if Your Majesty takes Xuzhou today, within ten days Cao Cao will surely come to contest it—even with seventy or eighty thousand men to hold it, you will still have worry."
translations.idiomatic: Yet the terrain is open land where swift cavalry can run free; if Your Majesty takes Xuzhou today, within ten days Cao Cao will surely come to contest it—even with seventy or eighty thousand men to hold it, you will still have worry."

sentences.zh: 不如取羽，全據長江，形勢益張，易為守也。

translations.literal: Better to take Yu, hold the Yangtze entirely, and the strategic situation will expand—easier to defend."
translations.idiomatic: Better to take Guan Yu, hold the Yangtze entirely, and the strategic situation will expand—easier to defend."

sentences.zh: 」權善之。

translations.literal: Quan approved.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan approved.

sentences.zh: 權嘗為其子求昏於羽，羽罵其使，不許昏；

translations.literal: Quan once sought a marriage alliance for his son with Yu; Yu cursed the envoy and refused the marriage;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan once sought a marriage alliance for his son with Guan Yu; Guan Yu cursed the envoy and refused the marriage;

sentences.zh: 權由是怒。

translations.literal: Quan from this was angry.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan from this was angry.

sentences.zh: 及羽攻樊，呂蒙上疏曰：「羽討樊而多留備兵，必恐蒙圖其後故也。

translations.literal: When Yu attacked Fan, Lü Meng submitted a memorial, saying: "Yu is attacking Fan yet has left many reserve troops—it must be because he fears Meng will plot against his rear.
translations.idiomatic: When Guan Yu attacked Fan, Lü Meng submitted a memorial, saying, "Guan Yu is attacking Fan yet has left many reserve troops—it must be because he fears I will plot against his rear.

sentences.zh: 蒙常有病，乞分士眾還建業，以治疾為名，羽聞之，必撤備兵，盡赴襄陽。

translations.literal: Meng is often ill; I beg to divide the troops and return to Jianye in the name of treating the illness—when Yu hears of it, he is sure to withdraw the reserve troops and send them all to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: I am often ill; I beg to divide the troops and return to Jianye in the name of treating the illness—when Guan Yu hears of it, he is sure to withdraw the reserve troops and send them all to Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 大軍浮江晝夜馳上，襲其空虛，則南郡可下而羽可禽也。

translations.literal: The great army will sail up the river day and night, strike his emptiness, and then Nan Commandery can be taken and Yu captured."
translations.idiomatic: The great army will sail up the river day and night, strike his emptiness, and then Nan Commandery can be taken and Guan Yu captured."

sentences.zh: 」遂稱病篤。

translations.literal: He then claimed his illness was grave.
translations.idiomatic: He then claimed his illness was grave.

sentences.zh: 權乃露檄召蒙還，陰與圖計。

translations.literal: Quan then openly issued a summons for Meng to return, secretly planning with him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan then openly issued a summons for Lü Meng to return, secretly planning with him.

sentences.zh: 蒙下至蕪湖，定威校尉陸遜謂蒙曰：「關羽接境，如何遠下，後不當可憂也？

translations.literal: When Meng reached Wuhu, Colonel Dingwei Lu Xun said to Meng: "Guan Yu is on our border—how can you go far down? Will not trouble follow afterward?"
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Meng reached Wuhu, Colonel Dingwei Lu Xun said to Lü Meng, "Guan Yu is on our border—how can you go far down? Will not trouble follow afterward?"

sentences.zh: 」蒙曰：「誠如來言，然我病篤。

translations.literal: Meng said: "It is truly as you say, yet I am gravely ill."
translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng said, "It is truly as you say, yet I am gravely ill."

sentences.zh: 」遜曰：「羽矜其驍氣，陵轢於人，始有大功，意驕志逸，但務北進，未嫌於我；

translations.literal: Xun said: "Yu prides himself on his fierce spirit and lords it over others; having just achieved great merit, his intent is proud and his will relaxed; he attends only to pushing north and has not yet been wary of us;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun said, "Guan Yu prides himself on his fierce spirit and lords it over others; having just achieved great merit, his intent is proud and his will relaxed; he attends only to pushing north and has not yet been wary of us;

sentences.zh: 有相聞病，必益無備。

translations.literal: when he hears you are ill, he is sure to grow ever more unprepared.
translations.idiomatic: when he hears you are ill, he is sure to grow ever more unprepared.

sentences.zh: 今出其不意，自可禽制。

translations.literal: Strike him now when he does not expect it, and of itself he can be captured and controlled."
translations.idiomatic: Strike him now when he does not expect it, and of itself he can be captured and controlled."

sentences.zh: 下見至尊，宜好為計。

translations.literal: When you go down to see Your Majesty, you ought to plan well."
translations.idiomatic: When you go down to see Your Majesty, you ought to plan well."

sentences.zh: 」蒙曰：「羽素勇猛，既難為敵，且已據荊州，恩信大行，兼始有功，膽勢益盛，未易圖也。

translations.literal: Meng said: "Yu has always been fierce and brave—he is hard to match as an enemy; moreover he already holds Jing Province, where kindness and trust are widely exercised; combined with his fresh merit, his courage and momentum grow ever greater—not easy to plot against."
translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng said, "Guan Yu has always been fierce and brave—he is hard to match as an enemy; moreover he already holds Jing Province, where kindness and trust are widely exercised; combined with his fresh merit, his courage and momentum grow ever greater—not easy to plot against."

sentences.zh: 」蒙至都，權問：「誰可代卿者？

translations.literal: When Meng reached the capital, Quan asked: "Who can replace you?"
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Meng reached the capital, Sun Quan asked, "Who can replace you?"

sentences.zh: 」蒙對曰：「陸遜意思深長，才堪負重，觀其規慮，終可大任；

translations.literal: Meng replied: "Lu Xun's thought runs deep and far; his talent can bear heavy responsibility; judging by his plans and considerations, in the end he can hold great office;
translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng replied, "Lu Xun's thought runs deep and far; his talent can bear heavy responsibility; judging by his plans and considerations, in the end he can hold great office;

sentences.zh: 而未有遠名，非羽所忌，無復是過也。

translations.literal: yet he has no distant fame—not someone Yu would fear; no one would be better than he."
translations.idiomatic: yet he has no distant fame—not someone Guan Yu would fear; no one would be better than he."

sentences.zh: 若用之，當令外自韜隱，內察形便，然後可克。

translations.literal: If you employ him, he should outwardly hide himself and inwardly observe the strategic situation—only then can Yu be taken."
translations.idiomatic: If you employ him, he should outwardly hide himself and inwardly observe the strategic situation—only then can Guan Yu be taken."

sentences.zh: 」權乃召遜，拜偏將軍、右部督，以代蒙。

translations.literal: Quan then summoned Xun, appointed him General of the Left Flank and Right Division Commander, to replace Meng.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan then summoned Lu Xun, appointed him General of the Left Flank and Right Division Commander, to replace Lü Meng.

sentences.zh: 遜至陸口，為書與羽，稱其功美，深自謙抑，為盡忠自托之意。

translations.literal: Xun arrived at Lukou, wrote a letter to Yu, praised his achievements as beautiful, deeply humbled himself, expressing the intent of utmost loyalty and placing trust in him.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun reached Lukou and wrote to Guan Yu, praising his victories while abasing himself in the humblest terms—conveying every appearance of loyal devotion and willing dependence.

sentences.zh: 羽意大安，無復所嫌，稍撤兵以赴樊。

translations.literal: Yu was greatly reassured in mind, no longer harbored suspicions, and gradually withdrew troops to march to Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu's suspicions were wholly allayed; he gradually pulled troops away to reinforce his siege of Fan.

sentences.zh: 遜具啟形狀，陳其可禽之要。

translations.literal: Xun fully reported the situation in a memorial, setting forth the essentials of how Yu could be captured.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun sent Sun Quan a full report on Guan Yu's disposition and laid out the key points for taking him.

sentences.zh: 羽得-{于}-禁等人馬數萬，糧食乏絕，擅取權湘關米；

translations.literal: Yu obtained Yu Jin and others' troops and horses numbering tens of thousands; grain and food were exhausted and cut off; on his own authority he took Quan's Xiang Pass grain;
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu had taken Yu Jin and tens of thousands of men and horses, yet his supplies were running out; without authorization he seized grain stored at Sun Quan's Xiang Pass depot;

sentences.zh: 權聞之，遂發兵襲羽。

translations.literal: Quan heard of it and thereupon sent troops to strike Yu.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan heard of this, he launched an attack on Guan Yu.

sentences.zh: 權欲令征虜將軍孫皎與呂蒙為左右部大督，蒙曰：「若至尊以征虜能，宜用之；

translations.literal: Quan wished to appoint General Who Pacifies the Barbarians Sun Jiao and Lü Meng as left and right Grand Commanders; Meng said: "If Your Majesty considers Pacifies the Barbarians capable, he should be used;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan meant to appoint General Who Pacifies the Barbarians Sun Jiao and Lü Meng joint Grand Commanders of the left and right wings. Lü Meng said, "If Your Majesty believes Sun Jiao is the better man, use him;

sentences.zh: 以蒙能，宜用蒙。

translations.literal: If Meng is capable, Meng should be used.
translations.idiomatic: If you believe I am the better man, use me.

sentences.zh: 昔周瑜、程普為左右部督，督兵攻江陵，雖事決於瑜，普自恃久將，且俱是督，遂共不睦，幾敗國事，此目前之戒也。

translations.literal: Formerly Zhou Yu and Cheng Pu were left and right commanders, commanding troops to attack Jiangling; though affairs were decided by Yu, Pu relied on his long service as a general and that both were commanders, and thus they were mutually at odds, nearly ruining state affairs—this is a warning before our very eyes.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Yu and Cheng Pu once served as joint commanders in the assault on Jiangling, Yu held final authority—but Cheng Pu, a veteran general who resented sharing equal rank, quarreled with him and nearly wrecked the campaign. That lesson is still before us.

sentences.zh: 」權寤，謝蒙曰：「以卿為大督，命皎為後繼可也。

translations.literal: " Quan came to his senses, apologized to Meng, and said: "I appoint you Grand Commander and order Jiao to follow as reserve—that will do.
translations.idiomatic: " Sun Quan saw the point, apologized to Lü Meng, and said, "You shall be Grand Commander; Sun Jiao may follow as your reserve.

sentences.zh: 魏王操之出漢中也，使平寇將軍徐晃屯宛以助曹仁；

translations.literal: When King Cao of Wei marched out of Hanzhong, he made General Who Pacifies Bandits Xu Huang encamp at Wan to aid Cao Ren;
translations.idiomatic: When King Cao Cao marched out of Hanzhong, he posted General Who Pacifies Bandits Xu Huang at Wan to reinforce Cao Ren;

sentences.zh: 及-{于}-禁陷沒，晃前至陽陵陂。

translations.literal: When Yu Jin was destroyed and lost, Huang advanced ahead to Yangling Slope.
translations.idiomatic: After Yu Jin's army was destroyed, Xu Huang pushed forward to Yangling Slope.

sentences.zh: 關羽遣兵屯偃城，晃既到，詭道作都塹，示欲截其後，羽兵燒屯走。

translations.literal: Guan Yu sent troops to encamp at Yancheng; once Huang arrived, he took a deceptive route and built encircling trenches, showing intent to cut off their rear; Yu's troops burned their camp and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu had posted troops at Yancheng. Xu Huang arrived, took a roundabout route, and dug entrenchments as though to cut off the enemy's retreat; Guan Yu's men burned their camp and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 晃得偃城，連營稍前。

translations.literal: Huang took Yancheng and moved his connected camps gradually forward.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Huang seized Yancheng and pressed his linked camps steadily forward.

sentences.zh: 操使趙儼以議郎參曹仁軍事，與徐晃俱前，餘救兵未到；

translations.literal: Cao sent Zhao Yan as Palace Attendant to participate in Cao Ren's military affairs; together with Xu Huang he advanced; the remaining relief troops had not yet arrived;
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao sent Palace Attendant Zhao Yan to advise Cao Ren and advance with Xu Huang, though the rest of the relief force had not yet come up;

sentences.zh: 晃所督不足解圍，而諸將呼責晃，促救仁。

translations.literal: The forces Huang commanded were insufficient to lift the siege, yet the generals shouted reproaches at Huang, urging him to rescue Ren.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Huang's command was too small to break the siege, yet the other generals berated him and pressed him to rescue Cao Ren at once.

sentences.zh: 儼謂諸將曰：「今賊圍素固，水潦猶盛，我徒卒單少，而仁隔絕，不得同力，此舉適所以敝內外耳。

translations.literal: Yan said to the generals: "Now the enemy siege has always been solid, floodwaters are still heavy, our foot soldiers are few and isolated, and Ren is cut off and cannot combine strength—this action would simply exhaust both inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yan told the generals, "The enemy ring is tight, the floods are still high, our numbers are few, and Cao Ren is cut off—we cannot strike together. A rash assault would only wear down both sides.

sentences.zh: 當今不若前軍逼圍，遣諜通仁，使知外救，以勵將士。

translations.literal: At present it is better to advance the army to press the siege, send spies to reach Ren, let him know of outside relief, to encourage officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Better to move up close to the siege, send agents through to Cao Ren, and let him know relief is coming—that will hearten the garrison.

sentences.zh: 計北軍不過十日，尚足堅守，然後表裡俱發，破賊必矣。

translations.literal: I reckon the northern army can hold no more than ten days and still defend firmly; then inside and outside strike together, and crushing the enemy is certain.
translations.idiomatic: The northern army can surely hold another ten days. Then we strike from within and without together, and the enemy will be broken for certain.

sentences.zh: 如有緩救之戮，餘為諸君當之。

translations.literal: If there is punishment for tardy relief, I will bear it for you all.
translations.idiomatic: If we are punished for moving too slowly, I alone will answer for it.

sentences.zh: 」諸將皆喜。

translations.literal: " The generals were all pleased.
translations.idiomatic: " The generals were all satisfied.

sentences.zh: 晃營距羽圍三丈所，作地道及箭飛書與仁，消息數通。

translations.literal: Huang's camp was about three zhang from Yu's siege; he made tunnels and arrow-carried messages to Ren; news was exchanged several times.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Huang pitched camp within three zhang of Guan Yu's siege lines, opened tunnels, and sent messages to Cao Ren by arrow and courier; word passed back and forth many times.

sentences.zh: 孫權為箋與魏王操，請以討羽自效，及乞不漏，令羽有備。

translations.literal: Sun Quan wrote a memorial to King Cao Cao, requesting to prove his loyalty by attacking Yu, and also asking that it not leak, lest Yu be on guard.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan wrote to King Cao Cao offering to attack Guan Yu in proof of his loyalty, and asked that the plan be kept secret so Guan Yu would not be forewarned.

sentences.zh: 操問群臣，群臣鹹言宜密之。

translations.literal: Cao questioned his ministers; the ministers all said it should be kept secret.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao consulted his ministers; all advised keeping the letter secret.

sentences.zh: 董昭曰：「軍事尚權，期於合宜。

translations.literal: Dong Zhao said: "In military affairs one values flexibility, aiming at what is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhao said, "In war one must be flexible and do what the moment requires.

sentences.zh: 宜應權以密，而內露之。

translations.literal: Outwardly one should agree with Quan to keep it secret, yet inwardly reveal it.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly agree with Sun Quan to keep silence; inwardly, let the news out.

sentences.zh: 羽聞權上，若還自護，圍則速解，便獲其利。

translations.literal: If Yu hears Quan has submitted, he will likely return to protect himself; the siege will quickly be lifted, and we will immediately gain the benefit.
translations.idiomatic: If Guan Yu learns Sun Quan has turned against him, he will hurry back to defend his own base—the siege will lift at once, and we gain the advantage.

sentences.zh: 可使兩賊相對銜持，坐待其敝。

translations.literal: This can make the two enemies face each other in mutual grip, sitting and waiting for their exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: We can set the two foes to grapple with each other and wait for both to wear themselves out.

sentences.zh: 秘而不露，使權得志，非計之上。

translations.literal: Keeping it secret and not revealing it, letting Quan succeed in his aim—that is not the top of strategy.
translations.idiomatic: To keep the secret and let Sun Quan have his way—that is poor strategy indeed.

sentences.zh: 又，圍中將吏不知有救，計糧怖懼。

translations.literal: Moreover, the officers inside the siege do not know relief is coming; counting grain, they are terrified.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the officers inside the siege do not know help is coming; counting their grain, they are growing desperate.

sentences.zh: 儻有他意，為難不小。

translations.literal: If there should be other intentions, the difficulty would be no small matter.
translations.idiomatic: If any of them turn disloyal, the trouble will be grave.

sentences.zh: 露之為便。

translations.literal: Revealing it is advantageous.
translations.idiomatic: It is better to disclose the news.

sentences.zh: 且羽為人強梁，自恃二城守固，必不速退。

translations.literal: Moreover Yu as a man is obstinate and overbearing; relying on two cities' solid defense, he will surely not withdraw quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Guan Yu is proud and stubborn; trusting in the strength of his two strongholds, he will not retreat in haste.

sentences.zh: 」操曰：「善！

translations.literal: " Cao said: "Good!
translations.idiomatic: " Cao Cao said, "Excellent!

sentences.zh: 」即敕徐晃以權書射著圍裡及羽屯中，圍裡聞之，志氣百倍；

translations.literal: " He immediately ordered Xu Huang to shoot Quan's letter into the siege and into Yu's encampment; those inside the siege heard it and their morale multiplied a hundredfold;
translations.idiomatic: " He at once ordered Xu Huang to shoot Sun Quan's letter into the besieged city and into Guan Yu's camp. When the garrison heard the news, their spirits soared;

sentences.zh: 羽果猶豫不能去。

translations.literal: Yu indeed hesitated and could not leave.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu, as predicted, wavered and could not bring himself to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 魏王操自雒陽南救曹仁，群下皆謂：「王不亟行，今敗矣。

translations.literal: King Cao Cao from Luoyang marched south to rescue Cao Ren; his subordinates all said: "If Your Majesty does not go quickly, we will be defeated now.
translations.idiomatic: King Cao Cao marched south from Luoyang to rescue Cao Ren. His officers all said, "If Your Majesty does not hurry, all is lost.

sentences.zh: 」侍中桓階獨曰：「大王以仁等為足以料事勢不也？

translations.literal: " Attendant-in-Ordinary Huan Jie alone said: "Does Your Majesty consider Ren and the others capable of gauging the situation of affairs?
translations.idiomatic: " Attendant-in-Ordinary Huan Jie alone said, "Does Your Majesty believe Cao Ren and the others can read the situation for themselves?

translations.literal: " He said: "They are.
translations.idiomatic: " He said, "They can.

sentences.zh: 」「大王恐二人遺力邪？

translations.literal: "" "Does Your Majesty fear the two men will slack their effort?
translations.idiomatic: " "Then does Your Majesty fear they will not give their full strength?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「不然。

translations.literal: " He said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: " He said, "No.

sentences.zh: 」「然則何為自往？

translations.literal: "" "Then why go in person?
translations.idiomatic: " "Then why go yourself?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「吾恐虜眾多，而徐晃等勢不便耳。

translations.literal: " He said: "I fear the enemy are numerous, and Xu Huang and the others' position is unfavorable, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: " He said, "I fear the enemy are too many, and Xu Huang and the others are badly placed—that is all.

sentences.zh: 」階曰：「今仁等處重圍之中而守死無貳者，誠以大王遠為之勢也。

translations.literal: " Jie said: "Now Ren and the others are in heavy siege yet hold to death without wavering—truly because Your Majesty from afar forms their strategic posture.
translations.idiomatic: " Huan Jie said, "Cao Ren and the others hold firm in the teeth of a siege because they know Your Majesty stands behind them from afar.

sentences.zh: 夫居萬死之地，必有死爭之心。

translations.literal: One who occupies a place of ten thousand deaths must have a heart to fight to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Men who stand in the shadow of death will fight as if death itself were nothing.

sentences.zh: 內懷死爭，外有強救，大王案六軍以示餘力，何憂於敗而欲自往？

translations.literal: Inwardly harboring fight-to-the-death resolve, outwardly having strong relief—Your Majesty need only deploy the six armies to show reserve strength; why worry about defeat and wish to go yourself?
translations.idiomatic: With that resolve within and strong relief without, Your Majesty need only muster the six armies to show your reserve strength. Why fear defeat and insist on going in person?

sentences.zh: 」操善其言，乃駐軍摩陂，前後遣殷署、朱蓋等凡十二營詣晃。

translations.literal: " Cao approved his words, and encamped his army at Mobei; before and after he sent Yin Shu, Zhu Gai, and others—twelve camps in all—to Xu Huang.
translations.idiomatic: " Cao Cao approved and halted at Mobei, dispatching twelve camps under Yin Shu, Zhu Gai, and others to join Xu Huang.

sentences.zh: 關羽圍頭有屯，又別屯四塚，晃乃揚聲當攻圍頭屯而密攻四塚。

translations.literal: Guan Yu had an encampment at the head of the siege, and separately four mound camps; Huang then loudly proclaimed he would attack the head encampment but secretly attacked the four mounds.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu had a camp at the head of his siege lines and four others at separate mounds. Xu Huang proclaimed he would strike the head camp but secretly assaulted the four mounds.

sentences.zh: 羽見四塚欲壞，自將步騎五千出戰；

translations.literal: Yu saw the four mounds about to be destroyed and personally led five thousand infantry and cavalry out to battle;
translations.idiomatic: When Guan Yu saw the four mound camps near collapse, he led five thousand foot and horse out to fight;

sentences.zh: 晃擊之，退走。

translations.literal: Huang struck them, and they retreated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Huang struck them and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 羽圍塹鹿角十重，晃追羽，與俱入圍中，破之，傅方、胡修皆死，羽遂撤圍退，然舟船猶據沔水，襄陽隔絕不通。

translations.literal: Yu's siege trenches and abatis were ten layers deep; Huang pursued Yu and entered the siege together with him, broke it; Fu Fang and Hu Xiu both died; Yu thereupon lifted the siege and withdrew, yet boats still held the Han River and Xiangyang remained cut off and impassable.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu's siege works stood ten layers deep with abatis. Xu Huang pursued him into the entrenchments, broke through, and Fu Fang and Hu Xiu were killed. Guan Yu lifted the siege and withdrew, but his fleet still held the Han River, and Xiangyang remained cut off.

sentences.zh: 呂蒙至尋陽，盡伏其精兵舳艫中，使白衣搖櫓，作商賈人服，晝夜兼行。

translations.literal: Lü Meng reached Xunyang, hid all his elite troops in the ships, had men in white clothing row the oars, dressed as merchants, marching day and night without rest.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng reached Xunyang, concealed his picked troops in the holds, put sailors in white to work the oars, dressed his men as merchants, and pressed on day and night without pause.

sentences.zh: 羽所置江邊屯候，盡收縛之，是故羽不聞知。

translations.literal: The riverside outposts Yu had set up were all captured and bound; for this reason Yu heard nothing and knew nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Every riverside outpost Guan Yu had posted was seized and bound, so he heard nothing of what was coming.

sentences.zh: 糜芳、傅士仁素皆嫌羽輕己，羽之出軍，芳、仁供給軍資不悉相及，羽言：「還，當治之！

translations.literal: Mi Fang and Fu Shiren had long resented Yu for slighting them; when Yu marched out, Fang and Shiren did not fully keep up with supplying army provisions; Yu said: "When I return, I will deal with them!
translations.idiomatic: Mi Fang and Fu Shiren had long resented Guan Yu for treating them lightly. When he marched out, their supply of provisions fell short, and Guan Yu said, "When I return, you will answer for this!

sentences.zh: 」芳、仁鹹懼。

translations.literal: " Fang and Shiren were all afraid.
translations.idiomatic: " Both men were terrified.

sentences.zh: 於是蒙令故騎都尉虞翻為書說仁，為陳成敗，仁得書即降。

translations.literal: Thereupon Meng had former Cavalry Commandant Yu Fan write a letter to persuade Shiren, setting forth success and failure; Shiren upon receiving the letter immediately surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng then had the former Cavalry Commandant Yu Fan write to Fu Shiren, laying out the stakes; Shiren surrendered as soon as he read the letter.

sentences.zh: 翻謂蒙曰：「此譎兵也，當將仁行，留兵備城。

translations.literal: Fan said to Meng: "These are deceptive hostages; one should take Shiren away and leave troops to guard the city.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Fan told Lü Meng, "This is a hostage gambit—take Shiren with you and leave troops to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 」遂將仁至南郡。

translations.literal: " He then took Shiren to Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: " He then brought Shiren to Nan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 麋芳城守，蒙以仁示之，芳遂開門出降。

translations.literal: Mi Fang defended the city; Meng showed him Shiren, and Fang thereupon opened the gates and came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Fang held the city. Lü Meng paraded Shiren before him, and Fang opened the gates and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 蒙入江陵，釋-{于}-禁之囚，得關羽及將士家屬，皆撫慰之，約令軍中：「不得干歷人家，有所求取。

translations.literal: Meng entered Jiangling, released Yu Jin from prison, obtained Guan Yu's and the officers' and soldiers' families, all comforted them, and issued orders to the army: "Do not intrude into people's homes or take anything.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng entered Jiangling, freed Yu Jin from captivity, and took charge of Guan Yu's officers, soldiers, and their families, treating them with kindness. He issued strict orders: "No soldier may enter a private home or take anything from the people.

sentences.zh: 」蒙麾下士，與蒙同郡人，取民家一笠以覆官鎧；

translations.literal: " A soldier under Meng, a fellow townsman of Meng's, took a conical hat from a civilian house to cover official armor;
translations.idiomatic: " One of Lü Meng's men—a fellow townsman—took a bamboo hat from a household to cover his government-issue armor;

sentences.zh: 官鎧雖公，蒙猶以為犯軍令，不可以鄉里故而廢法，遂垂涕斬之。

translations.literal: Though official armor is public property, Meng still considered it a violation of military law and that one cannot set aside the law because of hometown ties; he wept and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Though the armor was government property, Lü Meng still judged it a breach of military law and held that hometown ties must not override discipline; weeping, he had the man executed.

sentences.zh: 於是軍中震慄，道不拾遺。

translations.literal: Thereupon the army was shaken with awe; no one picked up lost items on the road.
translations.idiomatic: The army was awed into discipline; no one so much as picked up what lay in the road.

sentences.zh: 蒙旦暮使親近存恤耆老，問所不足，疾病者給醫藥，饑寒者賜衣糧。

translations.literal: Meng morning and evening sent close attendants to care for the aged, asking what they lacked; the sick were given medicine, the hungry and cold were granted clothing and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Morning and evening Lü Meng sent his close attendants to look after the elderly, asking after their needs; the sick received medicine, the hungry and cold received food and clothing.

sentences.zh: 羽府藏財寶，皆封閉以待權至。

translations.literal: The treasures stored in Yu's offices were all sealed and closed awaiting Quan's arrival.
translations.idiomatic: The treasures in Guan Yu's offices were sealed and left untouched until Sun Quan should arrive.

sentences.zh: 關羽聞南郡破，即走南還。

translations.literal: Guan Yu heard Nan Commandery had fallen and immediately fled south to return.
translations.idiomatic: When Guan Yu learned Nan Commandery had fallen, he turned south at once.

sentences.zh: 曹仁會諸將議，鹹曰：「今因羽危懼，可追禽也。

translations.literal: Cao Ren convened the generals to discuss; all said: "Now while Yu is in peril and fear, we can pursue and capture him.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Ren called his generals together. All said, "Guan Yu is shaken and in flight—we can run him down and take him.

sentences.zh: 」趙儼曰：「權遨羽連兵之難，欲掩制其後，顧羽還救，恐我承其兩疲，故順辭求效，乘釁因變以觀利鈍耳。

translations.literal: " Zhao Yan said: "Quan faced the difficulty of Yu's linked armies and wished to strike and hold his rear; seeing Yu return to rescue, he feared we would inherit their mutual exhaustion; therefore he spoke agreeably and offered his service, seizing opportunity from the change to observe profit and loss, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhao Yan said, "Sun Quan faced the difficulty of Guan Yu's united front and meant to strike his rear. Seeing Guan Yu turn back to rescue his base, he feared we would inherit their mutual exhaustion—so he spoke agreeably and offered his service, waiting on events to see where advantage lay.

sentences.zh: 今羽已孤迸，更宜存之以為權害。

translations.literal: Now Yu is already isolated and fleeing; it is better still to preserve him to be a harm to Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Now Guan Yu is isolated and on the run. Better to let him live and be a thorn in Sun Quan's side.

sentences.zh: 若深入追北，權則改虞於彼，將生患於我矣，王必以此為深慮。

translations.literal: If we press deep in pursuit, Quan will shift his watchfulness there and will bring trouble upon us; Your Majesty will surely give this deep consideration.
translations.idiomatic: If we press the pursuit, Sun Quan will turn his attention from Guan Yu to us and trouble will follow. The King will surely weigh that carefully.

sentences.zh: 」仁乃解嚴。

translations.literal: " Ren thereupon relaxed the alert.
translations.idiomatic: " Cao Ren then stood his men down.

sentences.zh: 魏王操聞羽走，恐諸將追之，果疾敕仁如儼所策。

translations.literal: King Cao Cao heard Yu had fled, feared the generals would pursue him, and swiftly indeed ordered Ren as Yan had advised.
translations.idiomatic: When King Cao Cao heard Guan Yu had fled, fearing his generals would give chase, he quickly ordered Cao Ren to follow Zhao Yan's counsel.

sentences.zh: 關羽數使人與呂蒙相聞，蒙輒厚遇其使，周遊城中，家家致問，或手書示信。

translations.literal: Guan Yu repeatedly sent men to exchange messages with Lü Meng; Meng always treated his envoys generously, toured the city, sent greetings to every household, or showed written letters as proof.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu sent envoys again and again to inquire of Lü Meng. Lü Meng always received them warmly, walked them through the city, sent greetings to every household, and sometimes showed them letters in his own hand as proof.

sentences.zh: 羽人還，私相參訊，咸知家門無恙，見待過於平時，故羽吏士無鬥心。

translations.literal: Yu's men returned and privately questioned one another; all knew their homes were unharmed and they were treated better than in ordinary times; therefore Yu's officers and soldiers had no will to fight.
translations.idiomatic: When Guan Yu's men returned, they questioned one another in private and learned that their families were safe and even better treated than before. Guan Yu's officers and soldiers lost all will to fight.

sentences.zh: 會權至江陵，荊州將吏悉皆歸附；

translations.literal: When Quan arrived at Jiangling, Jing Province's generals and officers all submitted;
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan reached Jiangling, the generals and officials of Jing Province all submitted;

sentences.zh: 獨治中從事武陵潘濬稱疾不見。

translations.literal: Only Chief Clerk Pan Jun of Wuling claimed illness and did not appear.
translations.idiomatic: Only Pan Jun, Chief Clerk of Wuling, pleaded illness and refused to appear.

sentences.zh: 權遣人以床就家輿致之，濬伏面著床席不起，涕泣交橫，哀哽不能自勝。

translations.literal: Quan sent men with a couch to his home to carry him in; Jun lay face down on the bed mat and would not rise, tears and weeping crossing his face, grief choking him beyond self-control.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan sent men with a litter to fetch him from his home. Pan Jun lay face down on the mat and would not rise, weeping until grief choked him beyond bearing.

sentences.zh: 權呼其字與語，慰諭懇惻，使親近以手巾拭其面。

translations.literal: Quan called him by his courtesy name and spoke with him, comforting and instructing with earnest sincerity, had a close attendant wipe his face with a handkerchief.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan addressed him by his courtesy name and spoke with earnest consolation; a close attendant wiped his face with a handkerchief.

sentences.zh: 濬起，下地拜謝。

translations.literal: Jun rose, came down from the couch, and bowed in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Jun rose, stepped down from the litter, and bowed in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 即以為治中，荊州軍事一以諮之。

translations.literal: He was immediately made Chief Clerk; all Jing Province military affairs were entrusted to his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan at once appointed him Chief Clerk and entrusted all military affairs of Jing Province to his judgment.

sentences.zh: 武陵部從事樊胄誘導諸夷，圖以武陵附漢中王備。

translations.literal: Wuling Department Attendant Fan Zhou incited and led the various barbarians, plotting to attach Wuling to King of Hanzhong Bei.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhou, Department Attendant of Wuling, incited the tribal peoples there and plotted to bring Wuling over to Liu Bei, King of Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 外白差督督萬人往討之，權不聽；

translations.literal: Outside officials reported recommending dispatching a supervising officer with ten thousand men to attack; Quan did not listen;
translations.idiomatic: Outside advisers recommended sending a commander with ten thousand men to suppress him; Sun Quan would not hear of it;

sentences.zh: 特召問濬，濬答：「以五千兵往，足以擒胄。

translations.literal: He specially summoned and questioned Jun; Jun replied: "With five thousand troops sent, it is enough to capture Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Pan Jun specially and asked his view. Pan Jun answered, "Five thousand men will be enough to capture Fan Zhou.

sentences.zh: 」權曰：「卿何以輕之？

translations.literal: " Quan said: "Why do you treat him lightly?
translations.idiomatic: " Sun Quan said, "Why do you make so little of him?

sentences.zh: 」濬曰：「胄南陽舊姓，頗能弄脣吻，而實無才略。

translations.literal: " Jun said: "Zhou is an old surname of Nanyang; he can rather play with words, but in truth has no talent or strategy.
translations.idiomatic: " Pan Jun said, "Fan Zhou is a Nanyang man of good family and can talk a fine game, but he has no real talent or strategy.

sentences.zh: 臣所以知之者，胄昔嘗為州人設饌，比至日中，食不可得，而十餘自起，此亦侏儒觀一節之驗也。

translations.literal: The reason I know this: Zhou once prepared a feast for men of the province; by the time noon came, food could not be obtained, yet a dozen or more had already risen—this too is proof from observing one section like a dwarf.
translations.idiomatic: I know this because he once gave a feast for men of the province: by noon the food still had not come, yet a dozen guests had already left. That, like judging a dwarf by one joint, tells you all you need to know.

sentences.zh: 」權大笑，即遣濬將五千人往，果斬平之。

translations.literal: " Quan laughed greatly, immediately sent Jun leading five thousand men; indeed he beheaded and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: " Sun Quan laughed aloud and at once sent Pan Jun with five thousand men; Fan Zhou was beheaded and the disturbance put down.

sentences.zh: 權以呂蒙為南郡太守，封孱陵侯，賜錢一億，黃金五百斤；

translations.literal: Quan made Lü Meng Administrator of Nan Commandery, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Chanling, granted him a hundred million coins and five hundred jin of gold;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan made Lü Meng Administrator of Nan Commandery, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Chanling, and granted him a hundred million coins and five hundred jin of gold;

sentences.zh: 以陸遜領宜都太守。

translations.literal: He made Lu Xun acting Administrator of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Lu Xun acting Administrator of Yidu.

sentences.zh: 十一月，漢中王備所置宜都太守樊友委郡走，諸城長吏及蠻夷君長皆降於遜。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, Fan You, Administrator of Yidu appointed by King of Hanzhong Bei, abandoned the commandery and fled; commandery city chief clerks and barbarian chieftains all surrendered to Xun.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Fan You, whom Liu Bei, King of Hanzhong, had made Administrator of Yidu, abandoned his post and fled; city magistrates and tribal chieftains throughout the commandery surrendered to Lu Xun.

sentences.zh: 遜請金、銀、銅印以假授初附，擊蜀將詹晏等及秭歸大姓擁兵者，皆破降之，前後斬獲、招納凡數萬計。

translations.literal: Xun requested gold, silver, and bronze seals to provisionally grant to newly submitted peoples; attacked Shu generals Zhan Yan and others and great clans of Zigui who held troops; all were defeated and surrendered; beheaded captives and recruits before and after totaled tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun asked for gold, silver, and bronze seals with which to provisionally invest newly submitted peoples. He attacked Shu generals such as Zhan Yan and the great armed clans of Zigui, defeating and accepting the surrender of all; kills, captures, and recruits before and after numbered in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 權以遜為右護軍、鎮西將軍，進封婁侯，屯夷陵，守峽口。

translations.literal: Quan made Xun Right Protector of the Army and General Who Pacifies the West, advanced his enfeoffment to Marquis of Lou, encamped at Yiling, and guarded the gorge mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan made Lu Xun Right Protector of the Army and General Who Pacifies the West, advanced his rank to Marquis of Lou, and posted him at Yiling to guard the gorge.

sentences.zh: 關羽自知孤窮，乃西保麥城。

translations.literal: Guan Yu knew himself isolated and bereft, and thereupon westward defended Maicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu saw that he was alone and desperate, and withdrew west to hold Maicheng.

sentences.zh: 孫權使誘之，羽偽降，立幡旗為像人於城上，因遁走，兵皆解散，才十餘騎。

translations.literal: Sun Quan sent men to entice him; Yu feigned surrender, raised banners and set up dummy figures on the wall, then stole away; his soldiers all dispersed—only a dozen or so horsemen remained.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan sent men to lure him in. Guan Yu feigned surrender, raised banners and dummy figures on the walls, then slipped away; his army dissolved until only a dozen horsemen remained.

sentences.zh: 權先使朱然、潘璋斷其徑路。

translations.literal: Quan had first sent Zhu Ran and Pan Zhang to cut off his escape routes.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan had already sent Zhu Ran and Pan Zhang to block his escape routes.

sentences.zh: 十二月，璋司馬馬忠獲羽及其子平於章鄉，斬之，遂定荊州。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, Zhang's Major Ma Zhong captured Yu and his son Ping at Zhangxiang, beheaded them, and thereupon settled Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Pan Zhang's Major Ma Zhong captured Guan Yu and his son Guan Ping at Zhangxiang and beheaded them; Jing Province was settled.

sentences.zh: 初，偏將軍吳郡全琮，上疏陳關羽可取之計，權恐事洩，寢而不答；

translations.literal: Initially, Lieutenant General Quan Cong of Wu Commandery submitted a memorial setting forth a plan by which Guan Yu could be taken; Quan feared the matter would leak and shelved it without reply;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Lieutenant General Quan Cong of Wu Commandery had submitted a memorial outlining how Guan Yu might be taken. Sun Quan, fearing a leak, filed it away without reply;

sentences.zh: 及已禽羽，權置酒公安，顧謂琮曰：「君前陳此，孤雖不相答，今日之捷，抑亦君之功也。

translations.literal: When Yu had already been captured, Quan set out wine at Gong'an, turned and said to Cong: "You earlier set forth this plan; though I did not reply, today's victory is nevertheless also your achievement.
translations.idiomatic: After Guan Yu was captured, Sun Quan held a feast at Gong'an and turned to Quan Cong, saying, "You proposed this plan before; though I gave no answer then, today's victory owes something to you as well.

sentences.zh: 」於是封琮陽華亭侯。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he enfeoffed Cong as Marquis of Yanghua Village.
translations.idiomatic: " He then enfeoffed Quan Cong as Marquis of Yanghua Village.

sentences.zh: 權復以劉璋為益州牧，駐秭歸，未幾，璋卒。

translations.literal: Quan again made Liu Zhang Governor of Yizhou, stationed at Zigui; before long, Zhang died.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan again made Liu Zhang Governor of Yizhou and posted him at Zigui; before long Liu Zhang died.

sentences.zh: 呂蒙未及受封而疾發，權迎置於所館之側，所以治護者萬方。

translations.literal: Before Lü Meng could receive his enfeoffment, illness broke out; Quan had him brought and lodged beside his own residence, and tried every method in treatment and care.
translations.idiomatic: Before Lü Meng could receive his title, he fell ill. Sun Quan had him brought to lodgings beside his own and tried every possible means to treat and nurse him.

sentences.zh: 時有加金鹹，權為之慘戚。

translations.literal: When needling was applied, Quan was deeply anguished for him.
translations.idiomatic: When acupuncture was administered, Sun Quan was stricken with grief for him.

sentences.zh: 欲數見其顏色，又恐勞動，常穿壁瞻之，見小能下食，則喜顧左右言笑，不然則咄□昔，夜不能寐。

translations.literal: He wished often to see Meng's countenance, yet feared disturbing him; he constantly peered through a hole in the wall. When he saw Meng could take even a little food, he would rejoice, turn to those beside him and laugh and talk; otherwise he would sigh in distress and could not sleep at night.
translations.idiomatic: He wanted to see Meng's face often but feared tiring him, so he regularly looked in through a pierced wall. If Meng could eat even a little, Sun Quan would be delighted and turn to his attendants with laughter; if not, he would sigh in anguish and lie awake all night.

sentences.zh: 病中瘳，為下赦令，群臣畢賀，已而竟卒，年四十二。

translations.literal: In the midst of illness he recovered slightly; Quan issued a general amnesty, and all the ministers congratulated him—yet afterward Meng finally died, aged forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Meng seemed to rally in his illness, and Sun Quan issued a general amnesty; the whole court rejoiced—but in the end Meng died, at forty-two.

sentences.zh: 權哀痛殊甚，為置守塚三百家。

translations.literal: Quan was extraordinarily grieved and sorrowful; he established three hundred households to guard and maintain the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan was stricken with grief and assigned three hundred households to guard and maintain his tomb.

sentences.zh: 權後與陸遜論周瑜、魯肅及蒙曰：「公瑾雄烈，膽略兼人，遂破孟德，開拓荊州，邈焉寡儔。

translations.literal: Later Quan discussed Zhou Yu, Lu Su, and Meng with Lu Xun, saying: "Gongjin was heroic and fierce, his courage and strategy surpassing others; he then broke Mengde, opened up Jingzhou—far and alone with scarcely an equal.
translations.idiomatic: Later Sun Quan discussed Zhou Yu, Lu Su, and Lü Meng with Lu Xun, saying, "Gongjin was heroic and fierce, his courage and strategy second to none. He defeated Cao Cao and opened up Jingzhou—few could rival him.

sentences.zh: 子敬因公瑾致達於孤，孤與宴語，便及大略帝王之業，此一快也。

translations.literal: Zijing, through Gongjin, gained access to me; when I feasted and spoke with him, he at once touched on the great outline of the work of emperors and kings—this was one delight.
translations.idiomatic: Zijing was introduced to me through Gongjin. At our first feast and conversation he spoke of the grand design of founding an empire—that was my first delight.

sentences.zh: 後孟德因獲劉琮之勢，張言方率數十萬眾水步俱下，孤普請諸將，咨問所宜，無適先對；

translations.literal: Later Mengde, relying on the momentum of having taken Liu Cong, loudly declared that he was about to lead several hundred thousand men by land and water together downstream; I broadly summoned all the generals and consulted them on what should be done—none stepped forward first to reply;
translations.idiomatic: Later Cao Cao, riding the momentum of Liu Cong's surrender, proclaimed that he would soon advance downstream with hundreds of thousands of men by land and water. I gathered all my generals and asked their counsel—not one spoke up first;

sentences.zh: 至張子布、秦文表俱言宜遣使修檄迎之，子敬即駁言不可，勸孤急呼公瑾，付任以眾，逆而擊之，此二快也。

translations.literal: until Zhang Zibu and Qin Wenbiao both said an envoy should be sent with a letter of submission to welcome him; Zijing immediately rebutted, saying this would not do, and urged me to hastily summon Gongjin, entrust him with the host, and meet the enemy and strike—this was a second delight.
translations.idiomatic: until Zhang Zhao and Qin Wenbiao both advised sending an envoy with a letter of submission to welcome him. Lu Su immediately objected, urging me to summon Zhou Yu at once, put the army in his hands, and meet the enemy in battle—that was my second delight.

sentences.zh: 後雖勸吾借玄德地，是其一短，不足以損其二長也。

translations.literal: Later, though he did urge me to lend territory to Xuande—that was one shortcoming; it was not enough to diminish his two strengths.
translations.idiomatic: Later he did urge me to lend territory to Liu Bei—that was his one flaw, but not enough to outweigh his two great strengths.

sentences.zh: 周公不求備於一人，故孤忘其短而貴其長，常以比方鄧禹也。

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou did not demand perfection in a single man; therefore I forgot his shortcoming and valued his strengths, often comparing him to Deng Yu.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou did not demand perfection in a single man, so I overlooked his flaw and prized his strengths, often comparing him to Deng Yu.

sentences.zh: 子明少時，孤謂不辭劇易，果敢有膽而已；

translations.literal: When Ziming was young, I thought him merely one who did not shirk hardship or ease, bold and resolute with courage alone;
translations.idiomatic: When Ziming was young, I thought him simply a man who did not shirk hardship, bold and courageous—nothing more;

sentences.zh: 及身長大，學問開益，籌略奇至，可以次於公瑾，但言議英發不及之耳。

translations.literal: when he grew to manhood, his learning broadened and increased, his strategy reached wondrous heights—he could rank next to Gongjin, but only in quick, brilliant discourse did he fall short.
translations.idiomatic: but as he matured his learning broadened and his strategy became remarkable—he could rank second only to Gongjin, though he could not match Zhou Yu's brilliant, ready speech.

sentences.zh: 圖取關羽，勝於子敬。

translations.literal: In plotting to take Guan Yu, he surpassed Zijing.
translations.idiomatic: In plotting to take Guan Yu, he surpassed Lu Su.

sentences.zh: 子敬答孤書云：『帝王之起，皆有驅除，羽不足忌。

translations.literal: Zijing replied in a letter to me: "When emperors and kings rise, each has obstacles to be cleared away; Yu is not worth fearing.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su wrote back to me: "When emperors and kings rise, each has rivals to be cleared away; Guan Yu is not worth fearing.

sentences.zh: 』此子敬內不能辦，外為大言耳，孤亦恕之，不苟責也。

translations.literal: " This Zijing could not accomplish within yet spoke grandly without—I also forgave him and did not press the blame harshly.
translations.idiomatic: " Lu Su could not accomplish this inwardly yet spoke boldly outwardly—I forgave him and did not hold him strictly to account.

sentences.zh: 然其作軍屯營，不失令行禁止，部界無廢負，路無拾遺，其法亦美矣。

translations.literal: Yet in establishing garrison camps and cantonments, he never failed in enforcing orders and prohibitions; within his command there was no neglect of duty, and on the roads nothing was left unpicked up—the excellence of his regulations was also admirable.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in organizing garrison camps he never failed to enforce discipline; within his command no duties were neglected, and nothing was left lying on the roads—the excellence of his system was admirable as well.

sentences.zh: 」孫權與-{于}-禁乘馬並行，虞翻呵禁曰：「汝降虜，何敢與吾君齊馬首乎！

translations.literal: " Sun Quan rode abreast with Yu Jin on horseback. Yu Fan shouted at Jin: "You surrendered captive—how dare you draw level with our lord's horse's head!
translations.idiomatic: " Sun Quan was riding side by side with Yu Jin. Yu Fan shouted at Jin, "You are a surrendered captive—how dare you ride level with our lord's bridle!

sentences.zh: 」抗鞭欲擊禁，權呵止之。

translations.literal: " He raised his whip wanting to strike Jin; Quan shouted and stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: " He raised his whip to strike Jin, but Sun Quan shouted and stopped him.

sentences.zh: 孫權之稱籓也，魏王操召張遼等諸軍悉還救樊，未至而圍解。

translations.literal: When Sun Quan declared himself a vassal, King Cao of Wei summoned Zhang Liao and the other armies all to return and rescue Fan; before they arrived the siege was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan declared vassalage, King Cao Cao recalled Zhang Liao and the other armies to relieve Fan, but before they arrived the siege had already been lifted.

sentences.zh: 徐晃振旅還摩陂，操迎晃七里，置酒大會。

translations.literal: Xu Huang led his troops in order back to Mobei; Cao went out seven li to welcome Huang and set out wine for a great assembly.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Huang marched his troops back in good order to Mobei. Cao Cao went seven li to meet him and held a great feast with wine.

sentences.zh: 王舉酒謂晃曰：「全樊、襄陽，將軍之功也。

translations.literal: The King raised his cup and said to Huang: "Saving Fan and Xiangyang—this is the general's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: The king raised his cup and said to Xu Huang, "The salvation of Fan and Xiangyang is your achievement.

sentences.zh: 」亦厚賜桓階，以為尚書。

translations.literal: " He also richly rewarded Huan Jie and made him Minister of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: " He also richly rewarded Huan Jie and appointed him Minister of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 操嫌荊州殘民及其屯田在漢川者，皆欲徙之。

translations.literal: Cao was displeased with the remnant people of Jingzhou and those doing frontier garrison farming in the Han River region, and wished to relocate them all.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao wished to relocate the remnant population of Jingzhou and those farming garrison lands along the Han River.

sentences.zh: 司馬懿曰：「荊楚輕脆易動，關羽新破，諸為惡者藏竄觀望，徙其善者，既傷其意，將令去者不敢復還。

translations.literal: Sima Yi said: "Jing and Chu folk are flighty and easily stirred; Guan Yu has just been defeated, and those who had done wrong hide and watch from concealment. If the good among them are relocated, that will wound their hearts and will cause those who have fled not to dare return.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi said, "The people of Jing and Chu are restless and easily swayed. Guan Yu has just been defeated, and wrongdoers are hiding and watching from the shadows. If you relocate the upright among them, you will wound their hearts and keep those who have fled from ever daring to return.

sentences.zh: 」操曰：「是也。

translations.literal: " Cao said: "It is so.
translations.idiomatic: " Cao Cao said, "That is right.

sentences.zh: 」是後諸亡者悉還出。

translations.literal: " After this, all who had fled returned.
translations.idiomatic: " After that, all who had fled returned.

sentences.zh: 魏王操表孫權為票騎將軍，假節，領荊州牧，封南昌侯。

translations.literal: King Cao of Wei memorialized that Sun Quan be made General of Fast Cavalry, with provisional credentials, Governor of Jingzhou, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: King Cao Cao memorialized the court to appoint Sun Quan General of Fast Cavalry with provisional credentials, Governor of Jingzhou, and Marquis of Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 權遣校尉梁寓入貢，又遣朱光等歸，上書稱臣於操，稱說天命。

translations.literal: Quan sent Commandant Liang Yu to present tribute, also sent Zhu Guang and others back, and submitted a memorial declaring himself Cao's subject, expounding upon the Mandate of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan sent Commandant Liang Yu to pay tribute, returned Zhu Guang and others to Wei, and memorialized the throne declaring himself Cao Cao's subject while expounding the Mandate of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 操以權書示外曰：「是兒欲踞吾著爐火上邪！

translations.literal: Cao showed Quan's letter to those outside and said: "This boy wants to seat me atop a brazier of fire, does he!
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao showed Sun Quan's letter to his advisers and said, "This boy wants to sit me on a brazier of fire, does he!

sentences.zh: 」侍中陳群等皆曰：「漢祚已終，非適今日。

translations.literal: " Palace Attendant Chen Qun and the others all said: "The fortune of Han has already ended—it is not only today.
translations.idiomatic: " Palace Attendant Chen Qun and the others all said, "The Han dynasty's mandate is spent—it did not end only today.

sentences.zh: 殿下功德巍巍，群生注望，故孫權在遠稱臣。

translations.literal: Your Highness's merit and virtue tower high; all living beings look to you in hope—therefore Sun Quan at a distance declares himself subject.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness's merit and virtue tower high, and all people look to you with hope—therefore Sun Quan, though far away, declares himself your subject.

sentences.zh: 此天人之應，異氣齊聲，殿下宜正大位，復何疑哉！

translations.literal: This is the response of Heaven and man, strange portents and unanimous voices—Your Highness ought to take the supreme throne; what doubt remains!
translations.idiomatic: This is the response of Heaven and the people, portents and unanimous acclaim—Your Highness ought to ascend the throne. What further doubt can there be!

sentences.zh: 」操曰：「若天命在吾，吾為周文王矣。

translations.literal: " Cao said: "If the Mandate of Heaven is with me, I shall be King Wen of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: " Cao Cao said, "If the Mandate of Heaven is mine, I shall be King Wen of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：教化，國家之急務也，而俗吏慢之；

translations.literal: Your servant Guang says: Instruction and transformation are the urgent business of the state, yet vulgar officers treat them lightly;
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang comments: Moral instruction is the urgent business of a state, yet petty officials treat it lightly;

sentences.zh: 風俗，天下之大事也，而庸君忽之。

translations.literal: customs and mores are the great affair of the realm, yet mediocre rulers neglect them.
translations.idiomatic: and customs are a great matter for the realm, yet mediocre rulers neglect them.

sentences.zh: 夫惟明智君子，深識長慮，然後知其為益之大而收功之遠也。

translations.literal: Only a wise and enlightened gentleman, with deep understanding and far-reaching plans, then knows how great is their benefit and how distant their harvest of achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Only a wise gentleman with deep insight and far-sighted planning can see how great their benefit is and how long before their full reward is reaped.

sentences.zh: 光武遭漢中衰，群雄糜沸，奮起布衣，紹恢前緒，征伐四方，日不暇給，乃能敦尚經術，賓延儒雅，開廣學校，修明禮樂。

translations.literal: Guangwu faced the Han in mid-decline, with competing heroes seething and boiling; he rose up from common cloth, continued and restored the former thread, campaigned in the four directions with not a day to spare—yet was able to earnestly honor classical learning, welcome and extend the company of the cultured and refined, open and broaden schools, and regulate and clarify ritual and music.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangwu faced the Han dynasty in decline and rival powers boiling over, he rose from common rank to restore the former order and campaign in every direction without a day's rest—yet still earnestly honored classical learning, welcomed scholars, expanded schools, and restored ritual and music.

sentences.zh: 武功既成，文德亦洽。

translations.literal: When military achievement was complete, civil virtue was also harmoniously fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Once his military achievements were secure, his civil virtue was fully established as well.

sentences.zh: 繼以孝明、孝章，遹追先志，臨雍拜老，橫經問道。

translations.literal: Succeeding him, Xiaoming and Xiaozhang urgently pursued the former design, attending at the Yong audience hall to bow to the aged, bearing the classics crosswise to inquire into the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaoming and Emperor Xiaozhang urgently followed his example, attending the Yong audience hall to honor the aged and study the classics under their teachers.

sentences.zh: 自公卿、大夫至於郡縣之吏，鹹選用經明行修之人，虎賁衛士皆習《孝經》，匈奴子弟亦游太學，是以教立於上，俗成於下。

translations.literal: From dukes, ministers, and grand masters down to the officers of commanderies and counties, all were selected and employed from among men clear in the classics and cultivated in conduct; the tiger guard warriors all studied the Classic of Filial Piety, and even sons of the Xiongnu came to study at the Imperial Academy—thus instruction was established above and custom took shape below.
translations.idiomatic: From dukes and ministers down to county clerks, all were chosen for mastery of the classics and upright conduct. Even the imperial guards studied the Classic of Filial Piety, and sons of the Xiongnu attended the Imperial Academy—thus instruction was established above and custom formed below.

sentences.zh: 其忠厚清修之士，豈唯取重於搢紳，亦見慕於眾庶。

translations.literal: Men of such loyal honesty and pure cultivation were not only held in esteem among the gentry, but also admired among the common multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Men of loyal honesty and pure conduct were admired not only among the gentry but among the common people as well.

sentences.zh: 愚鄙污穢之人，豈唯不容於朝廷，亦見棄於鄉里。

translations.literal: Men foolish, base, and foul were not only tolerated nowhere at court, but also cast off in village and neighborhood.
translations.idiomatic: Fools and the foul were not only unwelcome at court but rejected in their own villages as well.

sentences.zh: 自三代既亡，風化之美，未有若東漢之盛者也。

translations.literal: Since the Three Dynasties had perished, in the beauty of transforming customs none had matched the splendor of Eastern Han.
translations.idiomatic: Since the fall of the Three Dynasties, no age had matched the Eastern Han in the splendor of its customs.

sentences.zh: 及孝和以降，貴戚擅權，嬖倖用事，賞罰無章，賄賂公行，賢愚渾殽，是非顛倒，可謂亂矣。

translations.literal: From Emperor Xiaohe onward, imperial relatives monopolized power, favored minions held affairs in hand, rewards and punishments lacked rule, bribes walked openly, worthy and foolish were mixed in confusion, right and wrong inverted—it can be called disorder.
translations.idiomatic: From Emperor Xiaohe onward, imperial relatives monopolized power, favorites ran affairs, rewards and punishments lost all rule, bribery flourished openly, worth and folly were confused, and right and wrong inverted—it was chaos.

sentences.zh: 然猶綿綿不至於亡者，上則有公卿、大夫袁安、楊震、李固、杜喬、陳蕃、李膺之徒面引廷爭，用公義以扶其危，下則有布衣之士符融、郭泰、范滂、許邵之流，立私論以救其敗。

translations.literal: Yet still it endured unbroken without reaching extinction: above were such as Ministers Yuan An, Yang Zhen, Li Gu, Du Qiao, Chen Fan, and Li Ying, who spoke forthrightly in court debate and used public righteousness to support the realm in peril; below were such common-clothed scholars as Fu Rong, Guo Tai, Fan Pang, and Xu Shao, who established private discourse to rescue its collapse.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the dynasty still endured without falling utterly: above were ministers such as Yuan An, Yang Zhen, Li Gu, Du Qiao, Chen Fan, and Li Ying, who spoke bluntly in court and upheld public righteousness to brace the realm in peril; below were plain scholars such as Fu Rong, Guo Tai, Fan Pang, and Xu Shao, who voiced principled criticism to check the decline.

sentences.zh: 是以政治雖濁而風俗不衰，至有觸冒斧鉞，僵仆於前，而忠義奮發，繼起於後，隨踵就戮，視死如歸。

translations.literal: Therefore, though government was turbid, customs did not decline—to the point that some braved axe and halberd and fell stiff before the throne, yet loyalty and righteousness flared up behind them, following one upon another to execution, viewing death as homecoming.
translations.idiomatic: Thus though government was corrupt, custom did not decay—some were cut down before the throne for their boldness, yet others rose in loyal outrage, one after another marching to execution as though going home.

sentences.zh: 夫豈特數子之賢哉，亦光武、明、章之遺化也！

translations.literal: Was this due only to the worth of those several men? It was also the lingering transformation left by Guangwu, Ming, and Zhang!
translations.idiomatic: Was that only the merit of those few men? It was also the legacy of Guangwu, Emperor Ming, and Emperor Zhang!

sentences.zh: 當是之時，苟有明君作而振之，則漢氏之祚猶未可量也。

translations.literal: At that time, if a bright ruler had appeared to rouse and revive it, then the fortune of the House of Han might still have been beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: At that point, had a wise ruler risen to rally the realm, the Han dynasty's fortunes might still have been incalculable.

sentences.zh: 不幸承陵夷頹敝之餘，重以桓、靈之昏虐：保養奸回，過於骨肉；

translations.literal: Unhappily inheriting what remained after decline and exhaustion, compounded by the benighted cruelty of Huan and Ling: nurturing the wicked and perverse more than kin;
translations.idiomatic: Unhappily, the dynasty inherited decline and exhaustion compounded by the benighted cruelty of Emperors Huan and Ling: they nurtured the wicked more than their own kin;

sentences.zh: 殄滅忠良，甚於寇讎；

translations.literal: extinguishing the loyal and good more thoroughly than foreign foes;
translations.idiomatic: and destroyed the loyal and good more ruthlessly than foreign enemies.

sentences.zh: 積多士之憤，蓄四海之怒。

translations.literal: They accumulated the wrath of many scholars and stored up the anger of the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: They stored up the fury of scholars and the wrath of the realm.

sentences.zh: 於是何進召戎，董卓乘釁，袁紹之徒從而構難，遂使乘輿播越，宗廟丘墟，王室蕩覆，烝民塗炭，大命隕絕，不可復救。

translations.literal: Then He Jin summoned the barbarians; Dong Zhuo seized the opening; Yuan Shao and his kind followed in raising difficulty—thereby causing the imperial carriage to be driven afar, the ancestral temples reduced to ruins, the royal house overturned and ruined, the common people scorched in the flames, and the great destiny extinguished beyond recovery.
translations.idiomatic: Then He Jin summoned the barbarians, Dong Zhuo seized the occasion, and Yuan Shao and his allies raised rebellion—so that the imperial carriage was driven into exile, the ancestral temples lay in ruins, the throne was overturned, the people burned in misery, and the dynasty's mandate was lost beyond recovery.

sentences.zh: 然州郡擁兵專地者，雖互相吞噬，猶未嘗不以尊漢為辭。

translations.literal: Yet those in the provinces and commanderies who amassed troops and monopolized territory, though devouring one another, still never failed to take reverence for Han as their plea.
translations.idiomatic: Yet even warlords who amassed armies and carved out domains, though they devoured one another, still invoked loyalty to Han as their justification.

sentences.zh: 以魏武之暴戾強伉，加有大功於天下，其蓄無君之心久矣，乃至沒身不敢廢漢而自立，豈其志之不欲哉？

translations.literal: Take Weiwu—add to his fierce cruelty and harsh strength great merit in the realm; his heart long harbored thoughts of casting off the ruler—yet even to the end of his life he did not dare abolish Han and establish himself. Was it that his will did not desire it?
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao was violent, arrogant, and vastly meritorious; he had long harbored the wish to cast off the throne—yet even at his death he did not dare abolish Han and declare himself emperor. Was that because he did not want to?

sentences.zh: 猶畏名義而自抑也。

translations.literal: He still feared reputation and righteousness and restrained himself.
translations.idiomatic: He still feared public opinion and restrained himself.

sentences.zh: 由是觀之，教化安可慢，風俗安可忽哉！

translations.literal: Viewed from this, how can instruction and transformation be treated lightly—how can customs and mores be neglected!
translations.idiomatic: Seen in this light, how can moral instruction be treated lightly, or custom be neglected!
